title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第二十六: 太宗諸子
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第二十六: 太宗諸子 Volume 76 Biographies 26: Taizong's Sons

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 76 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: ○恆山王承乾 楚王寬 吳王恪 子成王千里 孫信安王禕

translations.literal: ○ Prince of Hengshan Chengqian; Prince of Chu Kuan; Prince of Wu Ke; his son Prince of Cheng Li Qianli; grandson Prince of Xin'an Yi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Prince of Hengshan Chengqian; Prince of Chu Kuan; Prince of Wu Ke; his son Prince of Cheng Li Qianli; grandson Prince of Xin'an Yi

sentences.zh: 濮王泰庶人祐 蜀王愔 蔣王惲 越王貞 子琅邪王沖

translations.literal: Prince of Pu Tai, Commoner You; Prince of Shu Yin; Prince of Jiang Yun; Prince of Yue Zhen; his son Prince of Langye Chong
translations.idiomatic: Tai Prince of Pu, Commoner You; Prince of Shu Yin; Prince of Jiang Yun; Prince of Yue Zhen; his son Prince of Langye Chong

sentences.zh: 紀王慎 江王囂 代王簡趙王福曹王明

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Shen; Prince of Jiang Xiao; Prince of Dai Jian; Prince of Zhao Fu; Prince of Cao Ming
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ji Shen; Prince of Jiang Xiao; Prince of Dai Jian; Prince of Zhao Fu; Prince of Cao Ming

sentences.zh: 太宗十四子：文德皇后生高宗大帝、恆山王承乾、濮王泰，楊妃生吳王恪、蜀王愔，陰妃生庶人祐，燕妃生越王貞、江王囂，韋妃生紀王慎，楊妃生趙王福，楊氏生曹王明，王氏生蔣王惲，後宮生楚王寬、代王簡。

translations.literal: Taizong's fourteen sons: Empress Wende bore the Great Emperor Gaozong, Prince of Hengshan Chengqian, and Prince of Pu Tai; Consort Yang bore Prince of Wu Ke and Prince of Shu Yin; Consort Yin bore Commoner You; Consort Yan bore Prince of Yue Zhen and Prince of Jiang Xiao; Consort Wei bore Prince of Ji Shen; Consort Yang bore Prince of Zhao Fu; Lady Yang bore Prince of Cao Ming; Lady Wang bore Prince of Jiang Yun; the rear palace bore Prince of Chu Kuan and Prince of Dai Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had fourteen sons. Empress Wende bore Gaozong, Chengqian Prince of Hengshan, and Tai Prince of Pu. Consort Yang bore Ke Prince of Wu and Yin Prince of Shu. Consort Yin bore the commoner You. Consort Yan bore Zhen Prince of Yue and Xiao Prince of Jiang. Consort Wei bore Shen Prince of Ji. Another Consort Yang bore Fu Prince of Zhao. Lady Yang bore Ming Prince of Cao. Lady Wang bore Yun Prince of Jiang. The rear palace bore Kuan Prince of Chu and Jian Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 恆山王承乾，太宗長子也，生於承乾殿，因以名焉。

translations.literal: Prince of Hengshan Chengqian was Taizong's eldest son; he was born in Chengqian Hall, and so received that name.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian, Prince of Hengshan, was Taizong's eldest son. He was born in Chengqian Hall and named for it.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，封恆山王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 (620) he was created Prince of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封中山。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7 (624) his fief was changed to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Chengqian became crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, Chengqian was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時年八歲，性聰敏，太宗甚愛之。

translations.literal: At that time he was eight years old, intelligent by nature, and Taizong loved him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He was eight years old, quick-witted, and Taizong doted on him.

sentences.zh: 太宗居諒暗，庶政皆令聽斷，頗識大體。

translations.literal: While Taizong observed mourning seclusion, Chengqian was ordered to hear and decide routine affairs, and he grasped the larger principles well.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's mourning seclusion he was entrusted with routine government and showed a sound grasp of affairs.

sentences.zh: 自此太宗每行幸，常令居守監國。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever Taizong went on tour he regularly had Chengqian remain behind to guard the capital and oversee the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever Taizong traveled he left Chengqian in the capital as regent.

sentences.zh: 及長，好聲色，慢游無度，然懼太宗知之，不敢見其跡。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved music and women and roamed idly without limit, yet he feared Taizong would learn of it and did not let his conduct show.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he took to pleasure and idle wandering, but fearing his father would find out he kept it hidden.

sentences.zh: 每臨朝視事，必言忠孝之道，退朝後，便與群小褻狎。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended court to conduct affairs he always spoke of loyalty and filial piety; after leaving court he would become intimate and familiar with his cronies.
translations.idiomatic: In court he preached loyalty and filial piety; once dismissed he caroused with his hangers-on.

sentences.zh: 宮臣或欲進諫者，承乾必先揣其情，便危坐斂容，引咎自責。

translations.literal: If palace officials wished to remonstrate, Chengqian would first gauge their intent, then sit upright with a composed countenance and blame himself.
translations.idiomatic: When palace tutors tried to remonstrate, he would read their mood, sit stiffly composed, and confess fault before they could speak.

sentences.zh: 樞機辨給，智足飾非，群臣拜答不暇，故在位者初皆以為明而莫之察也。

translations.literal: Quick-witted in argument and clever enough to cover wrongdoing, the assembled officials could not answer fast enough; those in office at first all thought him enlightened and none perceived the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Sharp in debate and skilled at masking misconduct, he outtalked his ministers, who at first took him for a capable heir and saw through him only later.

sentences.zh: 承乾先患足，行甚艱難，而魏王泰有當時美譽，太宗漸愛重之。

translations.literal: Chengqian had long suffered from a foot ailment and walked with great difficulty, while Prince of Wei Tai enjoyed contemporary renown for excellence, and Taizong gradually came to favor him more.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian had long been lame and walked with difficulty, while Prince of Wei Tai won contemporary praise; Taizong's affection gradually shifted toward Tai.

sentences.zh: 承乾恐有廢立，甚忌之。

translations.literal: Chengqian feared he might be deposed and set aside, and deeply resented Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian feared deposition and grew deeply jealous of Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰亦負其材能，潛懷奪嫡之計。

translations.literal: Tai also relied on his talent and secretly harbored a plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, confident in his gifts, secretly plotted to supplant his brother.

sentences.zh: 於是各樹朋黨，遂成釁隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon each built factions, and enmity arose between them.
translations.idiomatic: Each gathered partisans, and a bitter rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 有太常樂人年十餘歲，美姿容，善歌舞，承乾特加寵幸，號曰稱心。

translations.literal: There was a Director of Music entertainer over ten years old, handsome in appearance and skilled in song and dance; Chengqian especially favored him and called him Chengxin.
translations.idiomatic: A court musician in his teens, handsome and gifted in song and dance, won Chengqian's special favor; Chengqian called him Chengxin.

sentences.zh: 太宗知而大怒，收稱心殺之，坐稱心死者又數人。

translations.literal: When Taizong learned of it he was greatly angered, seized Chengxin and executed him, and several people died because of Chengxin.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong learned of the affair he was furious, seized Chengxin and had him killed, and several others died in the scandal.

sentences.zh: 承乾意泰告訐其事，怨心逾甚。

translations.literal: Chengqian believed Tai had informed against him and his resentment grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian believed Tai had informed on him, and his hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 痛悼稱心不已，於宮中構室，立其形像，列偶人車馬於前，令宮人朝暮奠祭。

translations.literal: Grieving Chengxin without end, he built a chamber in the palace, set up his image, and arrayed puppets, horses, and carriages before it, ordering palace women to offer morning and evening sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to stop mourning Chengxin, he built a shrine in the palace with the youth's image, set out effigies, horses, and carriages, and had palace women sacrifice to it morning and night.

sentences.zh: 承乾數至其處，徘徊流涕。

translations.literal: Chengqian often went to the place, pacing in circles and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian visited the shrine repeatedly, pacing and weeping.

sentences.zh: 仍於宮中起冢而葬之，並贈官樹碑，以申哀悼。

translations.literal: He also raised a tomb within the palace and buried Chengxin there, further granting him an office title and erecting a stele to express mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He even raised a tomb inside the palace, buried Chengxin there, granted him a posthumous office, and set up a stele in mourning.

sentences.zh: 承乾自此託疾不朝參者輒逾數月。

translations.literal: From then on Chengqian pleaded illness and failed to attend court audiences for months at a time.
translations.idiomatic: After that Chengqian often pleaded illness and skipped court for months on end.

sentences.zh: 常命戶奴數十百人專習伎樂，學胡人椎髻，翦綵為舞衣，尋橦跳劍，晝夜不絕，鼓角之聲，日聞於外。

translations.literal: He regularly ordered several dozen or a hundred household slaves to devote themselves to music and dance, learning the Hu topknot, cutting colored silks for dance robes, pole-climbing and sword-leaping, without cease day or night; the sound of drums and horns was heard outside every day.
translations.idiomatic: He kept dozens of household slaves drilling music and dance day and night—Hu-style topknots, silk dance robes, pole-climbing and sword dances—until drums and horns could be heard outside the palace daily.

sentences.zh: 時左庶子於志寧、右庶子孔穎達受詔輔導，志寧撰《諫苑》二十捲諷之，穎達又多所規奏。

translations.literal: At the time Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yu Zhining and Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent Kong Yingda received orders to guide him; Zhining composed twenty juan of Admonitory Garden to admonish him, and Yingda also submitted many remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: Left Mentor Yu Zhining and Right Mentor Kong Yingda were ordered to tutor him. Zhining wrote twenty juan of the Admonitory Garden; Yingda submitted many memorials of counsel.

sentences.zh: 太宗並嘉之，二人各賜帛百匹、黃金十斤。

translations.literal: Taizong praised them both and gave each a hundred bolts of silk and ten catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised them both and rewarded each with a hundred bolts of silk and ten catties of gold.

sentences.zh: 以勵承乾之意，仍遷志寧為詹事。

translations.literal: To encourage Chengqian's intent, he also transferred Zhining to be Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: To encourage Chengqian, he promoted Zhining to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，志寧以母憂去職，承乾侈縱日甚。

translations.literal: Before long Zhining left office on account of his mother's death, and Chengqian's extravagance and license grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhining left on mourning leave for his mother, and Chengqian's excesses worsened daily.

sentences.zh: 太宗復起志寧為詹事，志寧與左庶子張玄素數上書切諫，承乾並不納。

translations.literal: Taizong recalled Zhining as Grand Mentor; Zhining and Left Mentor Zhang Xuansu repeatedly submitted stern memorials, and Chengqian would not accept any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong recalled Zhining as Grand Mentor. Zhining and Left Mentor Zhang Xuansu sent sharp remonstrances again and again, but Chengqian ignored them.

sentences.zh: 又嘗召壯士左衛副率封師進及刺客張師政、紇干承基，深禮賜之，令殺魏王泰，不克而止。

translations.literal: He also once summoned the stalwart Deputy Commandant of the Left Guard Feng Shijin and the assassins Zhang Shizheng and Qagan Chengji, treated them with great courtesy and gifts, and ordered them to kill Prince of Wei Tai; they did not succeed and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned the strongman Feng Shijin, deputy commandant of the Left Guard, and assassins Zhang Shizheng and Qagan Chengji, honored them lavishly, and ordered them to kill Prince of Wei Tai. The attempt failed and the plot was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 尋與漢王元昌、兵部尚書侯君集、左屯衛中郎將李安儼、洋州刺史趙節、駙馬都尉杜荷等謀反，將縱兵入西宮。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Prince of Han Yuanchang, Minister of War Hou Junji, Central Commandant of the Left Garrison Li Anyan, Prefect of Yangzhou Zhao Jie, and Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law's Residence Du He in plotting rebellion, intending to unleash troops into the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he conspired with Prince of Han Yuanchang, Minister of War Hou Junji, Central Commandant of the Left Garrison Li Anyan, Yangzhou prefect Zhao Jie, and imperial son-in-law Du He to rebel and march troops into the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年，齊王祐反於齊州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Prince of Qi You rebelled at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 (643) Prince of Qi You rebelled in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 承乾謂紇干承基曰：「我西畔宮牆，去大內正可二十步來耳，此間大親近，豈可並齊王乎？」

translations.literal: Chengqian said to Qagan Chengji, "The palace wall on my western side is only about twenty paces from the Inner Palace — we are so close here; how can we be ranked with Prince of Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian told Qagan Chengji, "My palace wall on the west is barely twenty paces from the Inner Palace — we are that close. How can we be lumped together with Prince of Qi?"

sentences.zh: 會承基亦外連齊王，繫獄當死，遂告其事。

translations.literal: As it happened Chengji was also in secret contact with Prince of Qi, was imprisoned and faced execution, and thereupon informed on the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chengji was also secretly linked to Prince of Qi's rebellion, was jailed and condemned to death, and then revealed the plot.

sentences.zh: 太宗召承乾，幽之別室。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned Chengqian and confined him in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned Chengqian and held him in isolation.

sentences.zh: 命司徒長孫無忌、司空房玄齡、特進蕭瑀、兵部尚書李勣、大理卿孫伏伽、中書侍郎岑文本、御史大夫馬周、諫議大夫褚遂良等參鞫之，事皆明驗。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of Education Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, Special Grand Counselor Xiao Yu, Minister of War Li Jing, Chief Minister of Justice Sun Fuyan, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben, Censor-in-Chief Ma Zhou, Remonstrance Official Chu Suiliang, and others to join in examining him; the facts were all clearly verified.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Xiao Yu, Li Jing, Sun Fuyan, Cen Wenben, Ma Zhou, Chu Suiliang, and others to investigate. Every charge was proved.

sentences.zh: 廢承乾為庶人，徙黔州；

translations.literal: Chengqian was deposed as commoner and exiled to Qianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian was deposed to commoner status and banished to Qianzhou;

sentences.zh: 元昌賜令自盡，侯君集等咸伏誅。

translations.literal: Yuanchang was ordered to take his own life, and Hou Junji and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang was ordered to commit suicide, and Hou Junji and the rest were executed.

sentences.zh: 其宮僚左庶子張玄素、右庶子趙弘智、令狐德棻、中書舍人蕭鈞，並以材選用，承乾既敗，太宗引大義以讓之，咸坐免。

translations.literal: His palace staff — Left Mentor Zhang Xuansu, Right Mentor Zhao Hongzhi, Linghu Defen, and Secretariat Drafter Xiao Jun — had all been chosen for their ability; after Chengqian's fall Taizong reproached them on grounds of principle and they were all dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace mentors Zhang Xuansu and Zhao Hongzhi, Linghu Defen, and Secretariat drafter Xiao Jun had been chosen for talent; after Chengqian's fall Taizong rebuked them on principle and all were removed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，承乾卒於徙所，太宗為之廢朝，葬以國公之禮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Chengqian died at his place of exile; Taizong suspended court for him and buried him with the rites of a duke of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 19 (645) Chengqian died in exile. Taizong canceled court and buried him with ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 二子象、厥。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Xiang and Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Xiang and Jue.

sentences.zh: 象官至懷州別駕，厥至鄂州別駕。

translations.literal: Xiang rose to Vice-Prefect of Huaizhou, and Jue to Vice-Prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang became vice-prefect of Huaizhou; Jue became vice-prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 象子適之，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Shizhi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Shizhi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 楚王寬，太宗第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Kuan was Taizong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan, Prince of Chu, was Taizong's second son.

sentences.zh: 出繼叔父楚哀王智云。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to succeed his uncle, Prince Ai of Chu Zhiyun.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted to succeed his uncle Zhiyun, Prince Ai of Chu.

sentences.zh: 早薨。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初追封，無後，國除。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan period he was posthumously enfeoffed; having no heir, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was posthumously enfeoffed, but left no heir and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 吳王恪，太宗第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Ke was Taizong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Ke, Prince of Wu, was Taizong's third son.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，封蜀王，授益州大都督，以年幼不之官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and appointed Grand Governor of Yizhou; because he was young he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 (620) he was created Prince of Shu and named Grand Governor of Yizhou, but was too young to serve.

sentences.zh: 十年，又徙封吳王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) his fief was changed to Wu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，累授安州都督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was cumulatively appointed Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 12 (638) he was appointed governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 及將赴職，太宗書誡之曰：「吾以君臨兆庶，表正萬邦。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart for his post, Taizong wrote to admonish him, saying, "I rule the myriad people as sovereign and set the standard for all states.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left for his post, Taizong wrote to admonish him: "As sovereign I rule the myriad people and set the standard for all states.

sentences.zh: 汝地居茂親，寄惟籓屏，勉思橋梓之道，善侔間、平之德。

translations.literal: Your territory is that of a honored kinsman; you are entrusted as a bulwark of the realm — strive to reflect the bond between father and sons, and match the virtue of the Lords of Shen and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: You stand as a honored kinsman and bulwark of the realm. Strive to honor the bond between father and sons and match the virtue of the Lords of Shen and Bi.

sentences.zh: 以義制事，以禮制心，三風十愆，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Use righteousness to govern affairs and ritual to govern the heart; the three winds and ten faults must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Let righteousness govern your conduct and ritual govern your heart. Do not neglect the three winds and ten faults.

sentences.zh: 如此則克固盤石，永保維城。

translations.literal: If you do so you will firmly secure the foundation stone and forever preserve the wall of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Do so and you will secure the foundation stone and forever uphold the realm's wall.

sentences.zh: 外為君臣之忠，內有父子之孝，宜自勵志，以勖日新。

translations.literal: Outwardly show the loyalty of ruler and minister; inwardly keep the filial piety of father and son — you should steel your will and urge yourself to daily renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly show a minister's loyalty; inwardly keep a son's filial piety. Steel your will and renew yourself daily.

sentences.zh: 汝方違膝下，淒戀何已，欲遺汝珍玩，恐益驕奢。

translations.literal: You are now leaving my side; how endlessly you grieve at parting. I wished to send you rare treasures, but feared they would only feed pride and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: You are leaving my side, and your grief at parting is boundless. I would have sent rare treasures, but feared they would only feed pride and extravagance.

sentences.zh: 故誡此一言，以為庭訓。」

translations.literal: Therefore I admonish you with this single word to serve as instruction in the courtyard."
translations.idiomatic: So I offer this single admonition as your instruction from the courtyard."

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，拜司空、梁州都督。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Ke was appointed Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Ke was made Minister of Works and governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恪母，隋煬帝女也。

translations.literal: Ke's mother was a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's mother was a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui.

sentences.zh: 恪又有文武才，太宗常稱其類己。

translations.literal: Ke also possessed civil and military talent; Taizong often said he resembled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had both civil and military gifts; Taizong often said he resembled himself.

sentences.zh: 既名望素高，甚為物情所向。

translations.literal: His fame was already high, and he was greatly favored in public sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was already high and public sentiment favored him.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌既輔立高宗，深所忌嫉。

translations.literal: After Zhangsun Wuji had assisted in establishing Gaozong, he deeply envied and resented Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, who had helped place Gaozong on the throne, deeply envied Ke.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，會房遺愛謀反，遂因事誅恪，以絕眾望，海內冤之。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, when Fang Yi'ai's plot of rebellion occurred, Ke was executed on a pretext to cut off popular hopes; the realm considered it a grave injustice.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui, when Fang Yi'ai plotted rebellion, Ke was executed on a pretext to extinguish popular hopes. The realm regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 有子四人：仁、瑋、琨、璄，並流於嶺表。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Ren, Wei, Kun, and Jing; all were banished to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons—Ren, Wei, Kun, and Jing—all banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 尋追封恪為鬱林王，並為立廟。

translations.literal: Soon Ke was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yulin, and temples were established for them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was soon posthumously created Prince of Yulin and temples were established for the family.

sentences.zh: 又封仁為鬱林縣侯。

translations.literal: Ren was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Yulin county.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was also created Marquis of Yulin county.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，授襄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 (689) he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 不知州事，後改名千里。

translations.literal: He did not administer the prefecture and later changed his name to Li Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: He did not actually govern the prefecture and later changed his name to Li Qianli.

sentences.zh: 天授後，歷唐、廬、許、衛、蒲五州刺史。

translations.literal: After the Tianshou era he successively served as prefect of Tang, Lu, Xu, Wei, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianshou era he served successively as prefect of Tang, Lu, Xu, Wei, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 時皇室諸王有德望者，必見誅戮，惟千里褊躁無才，復數進獻符瑞事，故則天朝竟免禍。

translations.literal: At that time princes of the imperial house who had virtue and reputation were inevitably put to death; only Li Qianli was narrow-minded, impetuous, and without talent, and repeatedly submitted reports of auspicious portents, so he escaped harm throughout Empress Wu's reign.
translations.idiomatic: In those days talented imperial princes were routinely killed. Li Qianli alone escaped—narrow, impetuous, and untalented, he kept submitting reports of auspicious omens and so survived Empress Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，充嶺南安撫討擊使，歷遷右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he served as Pacification and Punitive Commissioner of Lingnan and was successively promoted to General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 3 (703) he served as pacification commissioner of Lingnan and was promoted to general of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 中興初，進封成王，拜左金吾大將軍，兼領益州大都督，又追贈其父為司空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration he was advanced to Prince of Cheng, appointed Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, concurrently Grand Governor of Yizhou, and his father was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration he was advanced to Prince of Cheng, made grand general of the Left Golden Guard and concurrent grand governor of Yizhou, and his father was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年，又領廣州大都督、五府經略安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the third year he also took charge as Grand Governor of Guangzhou and Commissioner for Pacification of the Five Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he also became grand governor of Guangzhou and commissioner for pacification of the five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 節愍太子誅武三思，千里與其子天水王禧率左右數十人斫右延明門，將殺三思黨與宗楚客、紀處訥等。

translations.literal: When the Resolute and Sorrowful Crown Prince killed Wu Sansi, Li Qianli and his son Li Xi, Prince of Tianshui, led several dozen followers to hack at the Right Yanming Gate, intending to kill Sansi's partisans Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jingmin killed Wu Sansi, Li Qianli and his son Xi, Prince of Tianshui, led dozens of men to hack at the Right Yanming Gate, intending to kill Sansi's allies Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna.

sentences.zh: 及太子兵敗，千里與禧等坐誅，仍籍沒其家，改姓蝮氏。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's forces were defeated, Li Qianli and Xi and the rest were executed for the crime, their household goods were confiscated, and their surname was changed to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's forces were defeated, Li Qianli, Xi, and their followers were executed, their property confiscated, and their clan name changed to Fu.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，詔曰：「故左金吾衛大將軍成王千里，保國安人，克成忠義，願除凶丑，翻陷誅夷。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict said, "The late Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, Prince of Cheng Li Qianli, guarded the state and settled the people, fulfilled loyalty and righteousness, wished to remove villains, yet fell instead into execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict said, "The late Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, Prince of Cheng Li Qianli, guarded the state and its people, upheld loyalty and righteousness, sought to remove villains, yet was executed instead.

sentences.zh: 永言淪沒，良深痛悼。

translations.literal: Words cannot express his ruin; grief is profound.
translations.idiomatic: His fall is beyond words; grief is profound.

sentences.zh: 宜復舊班，用加新寵，可還舊官。」

translations.literal: He should be restored to his former rank and granted new honors; he may resume his former office."
translations.idiomatic: Let his former rank be restored and new honors granted; let him resume his former office."

sentences.zh: 又令復姓。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to resume his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was also ordered to resume its original surname.

sentences.zh: 瑋早卒。

translations.literal: Wei died young.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died young.

sentences.zh: 中興初，追封朗陵王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Langling.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration he was posthumously created Prince of Langling.

sentences.zh: 子𥙆，本名褕，出繼蜀王愔。

translations.literal: His son Yi, original name Yu, was given in adoption to succeed Prince of Shu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, originally named Yu, was adopted to succeed Yin, Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，加銀青光祿大夫、秘書少監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 4 (710) he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，改封廣漢郡王、太僕卿同正員，薨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Prince of Guanghan commandery and Regular Associate Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 (725) he was transferred to Prince of Guanghan commandery and regular associate grand master of the Imperial Stud, and died.

sentences.zh: 琨，則天朝歷淄、衛、宋、鄭、梁、幽六州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: Kun, in Empress Wu's reign, successively served as prefect of Zi, Wei, Song, Zheng, Liang, and You, and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Kun served successively as prefect of Zi, Wei, Song, Zheng, Liang, and You and won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，嶺南獠反，敕琨為招慰使，安輯荒徼，甚得其宜。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era the southern barbarians rebelled; Kun was ordered to serve as Commissioner for Pacification, and in settling the remote frontier he was very much suited to the task.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengli the southern tribes rebelled. Kun was sent as pacification commissioner and handled the remote frontier admirably.

sentences.zh: 長安二年卒官，贈司衛卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an he died in office and was posthumously made Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 (702) he died in office and was posthumously made Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈張掖郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Divine Dragon era he was posthumously made Prince of Zhangye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Dragon Restoration he was posthumously created Prince of Zhangye commandery.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，以子禕貴，贈工部尚書，追封吳王。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, because his son Yi was honored, he was posthumously made Minister of Works and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 17 (729), because his son Yi had risen in honor, he was posthumously made Minister of Works and Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 璄，中興初封歸政郡王，歷宗正卿，坐千里事貶南州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Jing, at the beginning of the Restoration was enfeoffed as Prince of Guizheng commandery, served as Director of the Imperial Clan, was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Nanzhou on account of Li Qianli's affair, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was created Prince of Guizheng commandery at the Restoration, served as director of the Imperial Clan, was demoted to vice-prefect of Nanzhou over Li Qianli's affair, and died.

sentences.zh: 琨子禕。

translations.literal: Kun's son was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 禕少有志尚，事母甚謹，撫弟祗等以友愛稱。

translations.literal: Yi from youth had firm resolve, served his mother with great care, and was known for treating his younger brother Zhi and the others with brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yi was resolute, served his mother devotedly, and was known for brotherly care toward Zhi and his other younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年，為太子僕，兼徐州別駕，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jinglong he was Master of the Crown Prince's Household and concurrent Vice-Prefect of Xuzhou, with the rank of Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 4 (710) he was master of the crown prince's household and concurrent vice-prefect of Xuzhou, with the rank of Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 少繼江王囂後，封為嗣江王。

translations.literal: In youth he succeeded Prince of Jiang Xiao and was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he succeeded Xiao, Prince of Jiang, and was created heir prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，復為德、蔡、衢等州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he again became Prefect of De, Cai, Qu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) he again served as prefect of De, Cai, Qu, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開元後，累轉蜀、濮等州刺史。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan he was repeatedly transferred as Prefect of Shu, Pu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan he served repeatedly as prefect of Shu, Pu, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 政號清嚴，人吏畏而服之。

translations.literal: His administration was known for severity and clarity, and officials and commoners feared yet obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was stern and clear; officials and commoners feared him and submitted.

sentences.zh: 漸見委任，入為光祿卿，遷將作大匠。

translations.literal: He was gradually entrusted with responsibility, entered the capital as Minister of the Imperial Household, and was transferred to Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: As trust in him grew he entered the capital as Minister of the Imperial Household and was promoted to Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去官，起復授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's death, was recalled to service, and was appointed Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, was recalled, and was appointed prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又上表固請終制，許之。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial firmly requesting to complete mourning, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to complete full mourning, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改封信安郡王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 (724) he was transferred to Prince of Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 十五年，服除，拜左金吾衛大將軍、朔方節度副大使、知節度事，兼攝御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when mourning ended, he was appointed Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, Deputy Military Governor of Shuofang with authority over military affairs, and concurrently Acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 (727), when mourning ended, he was made grand general of the Left Golden Guard, deputy military governor of Shuofang with full authority, and acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部尚書，仍充朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Rites and still served as Military Governor of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Rites while continuing as military governor of the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 先是，石堡城為吐蕃所據，侵擾河右。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shibao Fortress had been held by Tibet and was harassing the lands west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao Fortress on the frontier had been held by Tibet and was harassing the lands west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 敕禕與河西、隴右議取之。

translations.literal: Yi was ordered to consult with Hexi and Longyou on taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was ordered to consult with the Hexi and Longyou commands on capturing it.

sentences.zh: 禕到軍，總率士伍，剋期攻之。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the army he marshaled the troops and set a date to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi reached the army he marshaled the troops and fixed a date for the assault.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此城據險，又為吐蕃所惜，今總軍深入，賊必併力拒守。

translations.literal: Someone said, "This fortress occupies a perilous position and Tibet cherishes it; if we now lead the whole army deep in, the enemy will surely combine their strength to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "The fortress sits on perilous ground and Tibet prizes it. If we drive the whole army deep in, the enemy will mass to hold it.

sentences.zh: 事若不捷，退則狼狽，不如按軍持重，以觀形勢。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, retreat will be disorderly; better to hold the army steady and observe the situation."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, retreat will be a shambles. Better to hold the army steady and watch how things develop."

sentences.zh: 禕曰：「人臣之節，豈憚艱險？

translations.literal: Yi said, "In the integrity of a subject, how can one fear hardship and peril?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "What subject's integrity shrinks from hardship and peril?

sentences.zh: 必期眾寡不敵，吾則以死繼之。

translations.literal: If it must be that numbers cannot match, then I will follow with my death.
translations.idiomatic: If numbers must tell against us, I will follow with my life.

sentences.zh: 苟利國家，此身何惜？」

translations.literal: If it profits the state, what is this body worth?"
translations.idiomatic: If it profits the state, what is one life worth?"

sentences.zh: 於是督率諸將，倍道兼進，併力攻之，遂拔石堡城，斬獲首級，並獲糧儲器械，其數甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urged the generals forward, marched by forced marches, attacked with combined strength, and captured Shibao Fortress; heads taken and grain stores and weapons seized were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove the generals forward by forced marches, attacked with combined strength, and took Shibao Fortress, capturing large numbers of heads, grain, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 仍分兵據守，以遏賊路。

translations.literal: He also divided troops to hold it and block the enemy's routes.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned the fortress and blocked the enemy's routes.

sentences.zh: 上聞之大悅，始改石堡城為振武軍，自是河、隴諸軍游弈拓地千餘里。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly pleased and first changed Shibao Fortress to Zhenwu Army; from then the armies of He and Long patrolled and expanded territory by more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and renamed Shibao Fortress Zhenwu Army. From then on the He-Long commands patrolled and expanded territory by more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 十九年，契丹衙官可突干殺其王邵固，率部落降於突厥。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Khitan yabgu Kedughan killed their king Shaogu, led the tribes to surrender to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 19 (731) the Khitan yabgu Kedughan killed King Shaogu and led his tribes to surrender to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣忠王為河北道行軍元帥以討奚及契丹兩蕃，以禕為副。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sent the Loyal Prince as Commander-in-Chief of the Hebei Field Army to attack the Xi and Khitan, the two tribes, with Yi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent the Loyal Prince as commander-in-chief of the Hebei field army against the Xi and Khitan, with Yi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 王既不行，禕率戶部侍郎裴耀卿等諸副將分道統兵出於范陽之北，大破兩蕃之眾，擒其酋長，餘黨竄入山谷。

translations.literal: The prince did not go; Yi led Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yaoqing and the other deputy generals in separate columns out north of Fanyang and greatly defeated the forces of the two tribes, capturing their chieftains while the remainder fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The prince did not take the field. Yi led Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yaoqing and other deputies in separate columns north of Fanyang, routed both tribes, captured their chieftains, and drove the rest into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 軍還，禕以功加開府儀同三司，兼關內支度、營田等使，兼採訪處置使，仍與二子官。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yi was given the merit rank of Opening the Government with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, concurrently Commissioner for Internal Support, Military Farms, and others, and Commissioner for Investigation and Disposition; his two sons also received offices.
translations.idiomatic: On return Yi was rewarded with the rank Opening the Government with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, concurrent posts over internal support and military farms, and a commission for investigation and disposition; his two sons also received offices.

sentences.zh: 禕既有勳績，執政頗害其功，故其賞不厚，甚為當時所嘆。

translations.literal: Yi already had achievements, and those in power were somewhat harmed by his merit, so his reward was not generous and people of the time sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power resented his merit, so his reward was thin—a fact much lamented at the time.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷兵部尚書，入為朔方節度大使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Minister of War and entered as Grand Military Governor of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22 (734) he was made Minister of War and grand military governor of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 久之，坐事出為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was dismissed for an offense and sent out as Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was dismissed for an offense and sent out as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄歷滑、懷二州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he successively served as Prefect of Hua and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served successively as prefect of Hua and Huai.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，拜太子少師，以年老仍聽致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince; because of old age he was still permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and, on account of age, was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷太子太師，製出，病薨，年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; when the appointment was issued he fell ill and died, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 2 (743) he was made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; when the appointment was issued he fell ill and died, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 上聞而痛惜者久之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he grieved and regretted it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for him a long while.

sentences.zh: 禕居家嚴毅，善訓諸子，皆有令命。

translations.literal: Yi at home was stern and strict, skilled in instructing his sons; all had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: At home Yi was stern and strict and trained his sons well; all won fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 三子：峘、嶧、峴，皆至達官，別有傳。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Huan, Yi, and Xian; all rose to high office and have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Huan, Yi, and Xian—all rose to high office and have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 祗，神龍中封為嗣吳王。

translations.literal: Zhi, in the Divine Dragon era was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Divine Dragon Restoration Zhi was created heir prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，為東平太守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao he was Prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 14 (755) he was prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，率眾渡河，凶威甚盛，河南陳留、滎陽、靈昌等郡皆陷於賊。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled he led his forces across the Yellow River; his ferocious power was very great, and Henan's Chenliu, Xingyang, Lingchang, and other commanderies all fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled he crossed the Yellow River in force. Henan's Chenliu, Xingyang, Lingchang, and other commanderies fell to him.

sentences.zh: 祗起兵勤王，玄宗壯之。

translations.literal: Zhi raised troops to aid the throne, and Xuanzong admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi raised troops for the throne, and Xuanzong admired him.

sentences.zh: 十五載二月，授祗靈昌太守，又左金吾大將軍、河南都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Zhi was appointed Prefect of Lingchang, also Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and Commander of Henan Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianbao 15 (756) he was made prefect of Lingchang, grand general of the Left Golden Guard, and commander of Henan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其月，又加兼御史中丞、陳留太守，持節充河南道節度採訪使，本官如故。

translations.literal: That month he was further made Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Chenliu, holding credentials as Military Governor and Investigation Commissioner of the Henan Circuit, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was also made acting vice censor-in-chief and prefect of Chenliu, with credentials as military governor and investigation commissioner of Henan, retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔以為太僕卿，遣御史大夫虢王巨代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict made him Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and sent Censor-in-Chief Prince of Guo Ju to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict made him Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and sent Censor-in-Chief Prince of Guo Ju to replace him.

sentences.zh: 濮王泰，字惠褒，太宗第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pu Tai, style name Huibao, was Taizong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, Prince of Pu, style name Huibao, was Taizong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 少善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，封宜都王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 (620) he was created Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封衛王，以繼衛懷王霸後。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Prince of Wei to succeed Prince Huai of Wei Ba.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 (621) he was advanced to Prince of Wei to succeed Ba, Prince Huai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，改封越王，授揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he was changed to Prince of Yue and appointed Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 (628) he was changed to Prince of Yue and named Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼領左武候、大都督，並不之官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he concurrently took charge as Left Martial Guard and Grand Governor, and in neither case took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was also named to the Left Martial Guard and grand governorship, but took neither post.

sentences.zh: 八年，除雍州牧、左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Governor of Yongzhou and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 8 (634) he was made governor of Yongzhou and grand general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉鄜州大都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred as Grand Governor of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633) he was transferred to grand governor of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，徙封魏王，遙領相州都督，余官如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, holding the governorship of Xiangzhou at a distance, his other offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was transferred to Prince of Wei with nominal governorship of Xiangzhou; his other posts remained.

sentences.zh: 太宗以泰好士愛文學，特令就府別置文學館，任自引召學士。

translations.literal: Because Taizong saw that Tai loved scholars and cherished literature, he especially ordered a separate Literary Academy set up at the princely mansion and allowed Tai to summon scholars himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tai's love of scholars and literature, Taizong set up a separate Literary Academy at his mansion and let him recruit scholars himself.

sentences.zh: 又以泰腰腹洪大，趨拜稍難，復令乘小輿至於朝所。

translations.literal: Because Tai's waist and belly were large and bowing was somewhat difficult, he was again allowed to ride in a small carriage to the place of court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tai's girth made bowing difficult, he was allowed a small carriage to the place of court audience.

sentences.zh: 其寵異如此。

translations.literal: His favor and distinction were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，司馬蘇勖以自古名王多引賓客，以著述為美，勸泰奏請撰《括地志》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Director of the Princely Mansion Su Xu, noting that famous princes since antiquity often gathered guests and took compiling writings as a beauty, urged Tai to memorialize requesting to compile Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 12 (638) mansion director Su Xu, noting that famous princes since antiquity gathered guests and took compiling works as an honor, urged Tai to request compiling the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm.

sentences.zh: 泰遂奏引著作郎蕭德言、秘書郎顧胤、記室參軍蔣亞卿、功曹參軍謝偃等就府修撰。

translations.literal: Tai thereupon memorialized and summoned Compiler Xiao Deyan, Secretariat Clerk Gu Yin, Recorder Jiang Yaqing, Merit Officer Xie Yan, and others to compile at the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Tai memorialized and summoned compiler Xiao Deyan, secretariat clerk Gu Yin, recorder Jiang Yaqing, merit officer Xie Yan, and others to compile at his mansion.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太宗幸泰延康坊宅，因曲赦雍州及長安大辟罪已下，免延康坊百姓無出今年租賦，又賜泰府官僚帛有差。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Taizong visited Tai's residence in Yan'ang Ward and on that occasion granted a special pardon in Yongzhou and Chang'an for capital crimes and below, exempted the people of Yan'ang Ward from this year's rent and tax levies, and bestowed graded gifts of silk on Tai's mansion officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 14 (640) Taizong visited Tai's Yan'ang Ward residence, granted a special pardon in Yongzhou and Chang'an for capital crimes and below, exempted Yan'ang Ward from that year's rent and taxes, and gave graded gifts of silk to Tai's staff.

sentences.zh: 十五年，泰撰《括地志》功畢，表上之，詔令付秘閣，賜泰物萬段，蕭德言等咸加給賜物。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Tai completed the work on Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm, submitted it in a memorial, and an edict ordered it deposited in the secret archive and gave Tai ten thousand items in gifts; Xiao Deyan and the rest also received additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 15 (641) Tai completed the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm and submitted it. An edict ordered it deposited in the secret archive and gave Tai ten thousand gifts; Xiao Deyan and the others received additional rewards.

sentences.zh: 俄又每月給泰料物，有逾於皇太子。

translations.literal: Soon monthly supplies of goods to Tai exceeded those of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tai's monthly supplies exceeded the crown prince's.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 太宗又令泰入居武德殿，侍中魏徵上奏曰：「伏見敕旨，令魏王泰移居武德殿。

translations.literal: Taizong also ordered Tai to move into Wude Hall; Attendant-in-Ordinary Wei Zheng submitted a memorial saying, "I have seen the imperial order directing Prince of Wei Tai to move to Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also ordered Tai to move into Wude Hall. Attendant-in-ordinary Wei Zheng submitted a memorial: "I have seen the order directing Prince of Wei Tai to move to Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 此殿在內，處所寬閒，參奉往來，極為便近。

translations.literal: This hall is inside the palace, the quarters spacious and open; coming and going to attend is extremely convenient and near.
translations.idiomatic: The hall lies inside the palace, spacious and convenient for attendance.

sentences.zh: 但魏王既是愛子，陛下常欲其安全，每事抑其驕奢，不處嫌疑之地。

translations.literal: But Prince of Wei is a beloved son; Your Majesty constantly wishes him secure and in every matter restrains his pride and extravagance, not placing him in a position of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Prince of Wei is a beloved son whom Your Majesty constantly wishes secure, restraining pride and extravagance and keeping him from suspicious ground.

sentences.zh: 今移此殿，便在東宮之西，海陵昔居，時人以為不可。

translations.literal: To move him to this hall now places him west of the Eastern Palace; when Prince Hailing once lived there, people at the time thought it improper.
translations.idiomatic: Moving him there now places him west of the Eastern Palace. When Prince Hailing once lived there, people thought it improper.

sentences.zh: 雖時與事異，猶恐人之多言。

translations.literal: Though times and affairs differ, one still fears that people will speak much.
translations.idiomatic: Though times differ, one still fears much talk.

sentences.zh: 又王之本心，亦不安息，既能以寵為懼，伏願成人之美。

translations.literal: Moreover the prince's own heart is also not at peace; since he can take favor as cause for fear, I venture to hope you will fulfill the beauty of his maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the prince's own heart cannot be at peace. Since favor itself can frighten him, I venture to hope Your Majesty will help him become a man.

sentences.zh: 明早是朔日，或恐未得面陳，愚慮有疑，不敢寧寢，輕干聽覺，追深顫慄。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow morning is the first day of the month; I fear I may not be able to state this face to face. Having doubts in foolish thought, I dare not rest in sleep and lightly intrude on Your Majesty's hearing; I pursue this with deep trembling."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow is the first of the month and I may not be able to speak face to face. Troubled by doubt, I dare not sleep and lightly intrude on Your Majesty's hearing; I submit this in deep trembling."

sentences.zh: 太宗並納其言。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted the words of both.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted both men's counsel.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子承乾有足疾，泰潛有奪嫡之意，招駙馬都尉柴令武、房遺愛等二十餘人，厚加贈遺，寄以腹心。

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Chengqian had a foot ailment; Tai secretly had the intent to seize the succession and recruited Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law's Residence Chai Lingwu, Fang Yi'ai, and more than twenty others, giving them generous gifts and entrusting them as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengqian was lame; Tai secretly plotted for the succession, recruiting imperial son-in-law Chai Lingwu, Fang Yi'ai, and more than twenty others with lavish gifts as his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎韋挺、工部尚書杜楚客相繼攝泰府事，二人俱為泰要結朝臣，津通賂遺。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Wei Ting and Minister of Works Du Chuke successively acted in charge of Tai's mansion affairs; both worked to win over court officials for Tai and opened channels for bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Wei Ting and Minister of Works Du Chuke successively ran Tai's mansion; both worked to win court officials and channel bribes.

sentences.zh: 文武群官，各有附托，自為朋黨。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials each had attachments and formed factions of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials each attached themselves and formed factions.

sentences.zh: 承乾懼其凌奪，陰遣人詐稱泰府典簽，詣玄武門為泰進封事。

translations.literal: Chengqian feared Tai would overpower him and secretly sent men posing as recorders of Tai's mansion to present a sealed memorial at Xuanwu Gate reporting Tai's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Tai would overpower him, Chengqian secretly sent men posing as Tai's mansion recorders to present a sealed memorial at Xuanwu Gate denouncing Tai.

sentences.zh: 太宗省之，其書皆言泰之罪狀，太宗知其詐而捕之，不獲。

translations.literal: When Taizong examined it, the document entirely listed Tai's offenses; Taizong knew it was fraudulent and sought to seize the men but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong read it and found only charges against Tai. Knowing the fraud, he tried to seize the men but failed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，承乾敗，太宗面加譴讓。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Chengqian was defeated; Taizong reproached him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 (643) Chengqian's plot collapsed; Taizong reproached him in person.

sentences.zh: 承乾曰：「臣貴為太子，更何所求？

translations.literal: Chengqian said, "I am honored as crown prince — what more is there to seek?
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian said, "I am crown prince—what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 但為泰所圖，特與朝臣謀自安之道。

translations.literal: It was only that Tai plotted against me, and I specially joined court officials in planning a way to secure myself.
translations.idiomatic: Tai plotted against me, and I joined court officials only to find a way to secure myself.

sentences.zh: 不逞之人，遂教臣為不軌之事。

translations.literal: Unruly men thereupon taught me to do improper deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Unruly men then taught me improper deeds.

sentences.zh: 今若以泰為太子，所謂落其度內。」

translations.literal: If you now make Tai crown prince, that is what is called falling within his measure."
translations.idiomatic: If you now make Tai crown prince, that is exactly what he has been scheming for."

sentences.zh: 太宗因謂侍臣曰：「承乾言亦是。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon said to the attending officials, "Chengqian's words also have a point.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then told his ministers, "Chengqian has a point.

sentences.zh: 我若立泰，便是儲君之位可經求而得耳。

translations.literal: If I establish Tai, then the position of heir can be sought and obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If I make Tai heir, the succession becomes something to be schemed for.

sentences.zh: 泰立，承乾、晉王皆不存；

translations.literal: If Tai is established, Chengqian and Prince of Jin will not survive;
translations.idiomatic: If Tai is made heir, Chengqian and Prince of Jin will not survive;

sentences.zh: 晉王立，泰共承乾可無恙也。」

translations.literal: if Prince of Jin is established, Tai together with Chengqian can be unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: if Prince of Jin is made heir, Tai and Chengqian can both be safe."

sentences.zh: 乃幽泰於將作監，下詔曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Tai was confined at the Directorate of Palace Construction, and an edict was issued:
translations.idiomatic: Tai was confined at the Directorate of Palace Construction and an edict was issued:

sentences.zh: 朕聞生育品物，莫大乎天地；

translations.literal: I have heard that in begetting and nurturing the myriad things, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in begetting and nurturing the myriad things, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 愛敬罔極，莫重乎君親。

translations.literal: in love and reverence without limit, nothing is weightier than sovereign and parent.
translations.idiomatic: in love and reverence without limit, nothing is weightier than sovereign and parent.

sentences.zh: 是故為臣貴於盡忠，虧之者有罰；

translations.literal: Therefore for a minister the precious thing is full loyalty; those who fail in it have punishment.
translations.idiomatic: For a minister the precious thing is full loyalty; failure brings punishment.

sentences.zh: 為子在於行孝，違之者必誅。

translations.literal: For a son the thing lies in practicing filial piety; those who violate it must be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: For a son the thing lies in filial piety; violation brings death.

sentences.zh: 大則肆諸市朝，小則終貽黜辱。

translations.literal: In great cases one is exposed in the marketplace and court; in small cases one ends by bearing dismissal and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Great offenses are exposed in marketplace and court; lesser ones end in dismissal and shame.

sentences.zh: 雍州牧、相州都督、左武候大將軍魏王泰，朕之愛子，實所鍾心。

translations.literal: Governor of Yongzhou, Governor of Xiangzhou, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Prince of Wei Tai is my beloved son, in whom my heart is truly set.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Yongzhou, governor of Xiangzhou, grand general of the Left Martial Guard Prince of Wei Tai is my beloved son, in whom my heart is set.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰令，頗好文學，恩遇極於崇重，爵位逾於寵章。

translations.literal: Clever and bright from childhood, he quite loved literature; favor exceeded the utmost in honor, and rank and title surpassed ordinary marks of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood and fond of letters, he received favor beyond ordinary honor and rank beyond ordinary grace.

sentences.zh: 不思聖哲之誡，自構驕僭之咎，惑讒諛之言，信離間之說。

translations.literal: He did not reflect on the admonitions of the sage, himself constructed the fault of arrogance and overstepping, believed the words of slander and flattery, and trusted talk of sowing division.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the sage's admonitions, built arrogance and overreach, believed slander and flattery, and trusted talk meant to divide.

sentences.zh: 以承乾雖居長嫡，久纏痾恙，潛有代宗之望，靡思孝義之則。

translations.literal: Though Chengqian as eldest legitimate son had long been afflicted with illness, he secretly harbored the hope of replacing the heir and did not think on the norms of filial piety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chengqian as eldest legitimate son had long been ill, he secretly hoped to replace the heir and ignored filial and righteous norms.

sentences.zh: 承乾懼其凌奪，泰亦日增猜阻，爭結朝士，競引凶人。

translations.literal: Chengqian feared Tai would overpower him; Tai also daily increased suspicion and obstruction, each winning court gentlemen and competing to draw in wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian feared Tai would overpower him; Tai daily grew more suspicious. Each won court gentlemen and drew in wicked men.

sentences.zh: 遂使文武之官，各有托附；

translations.literal: Thereupon civil and military officials each had attachments;
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials each took sides;

sentences.zh: 親戚之內，分為朋黨。

translations.literal: within kinsmen, factions divided.
translations.idiomatic: within the family, factions divided.

sentences.zh: 朕志存公道，義在無偏，彰厥巨釁，兩從廢黜。

translations.literal: My will rests in impartial justice; my righteousness lies in having no partiality — I make manifest their great crimes and dismiss both.
translations.idiomatic: My will rests in justice; my righteousness in impartiality. I make manifest their great crimes and dismiss both.

sentences.zh: 非惟作則四海，亦乃貽范百代。

translations.literal: This is not only to set a standard for the four seas but also to leave a model for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: This sets a standard not only for the four seas but for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 可解泰雍州牧、相州都督、左武候大將軍，降封東萊郡王。

translations.literal: Tai may be removed as Governor of Yongzhou, Governor of Xiangzhou, and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and demoted to Prince of Donglai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let Tai be removed as governor of Yongzhou, governor of Xiangzhou, and grand general of the Left Martial Guard, and demoted to Prince of Donglai commandery.

sentences.zh: 太宗因謂侍臣曰：「自今太子不道，籓王窺嗣者，兩棄之。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon said to the attending officials, "From now on, if the crown prince is unprincipled or a territorial prince covets the succession, both are to be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then told his ministers, "From now on, if a crown prince is unprincipled or a territorial prince covets the succession, both are to be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 傳之子孫，以為永制。」

translations.literal: Transmit this to sons and grandsons as an everlasting rule."
translations.idiomatic: Transmit this to sons and grandsons as an everlasting rule."

sentences.zh: 尋改封泰為順陽王，徙居均州之鄖鄉縣。

translations.literal: Soon Tai was changed to Prince of Shunyang and moved to Yunxiang county in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tai was changed to Prince of Shunyang and moved to Yunxiang in Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗後嘗持泰所上表謂近臣曰：「泰文辭美麗，豈非才士。

translations.literal: Later Taizong once held the memorial Tai had submitted and said to close officials, "Tai's literary style is beautiful — is he not a man of talent?
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong once held a memorial Tai had submitted and told close officials, "Tai's prose is beautiful—is he not a man of talent?

sentences.zh: 我中心念泰，卿等所知。

translations.literal: In my heart I think of Tai — you all know this.
translations.idiomatic: In my heart I still think of Tai—you all know this.

sentences.zh: 但社稷之計，斷割恩寵，責其居外者，亦是兩全也。」

translations.literal: But for the plan of the altars of soil and grain, I severally cut off favor and love and charge him to live outside — this is also securing both sides."
translations.idiomatic: But for the sake of the altars of state I sever favor and charge him to live outside—that too is securing both sides."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進封濮王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was advanced to Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 21 (647) he was advanced to Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，為泰開府置僚屬，車服羞膳，特加優異。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, an office was opened for Tai with staff; carriages, robes, and provisions were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne he opened an office for Tai with staff; carriages, robes, and provisions were especially generous.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，薨於鄖鄉，年三十有五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he died at Yunxiang, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 3 (652) he died at Yunxiang, aged thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、雍州牧，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Minister and Governor of Yongzhou, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Minister and governor of Yongzhou, with posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 文集二十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings were twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 二子欣、徽。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Xin and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Xin and Hui.

sentences.zh: 欣封嗣濮王，徽封新安郡王。

translations.literal: Xin was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Pu; Hui was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was created Heir Prince of Pu; Hui was created Prince of Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 欣，則天初陷酷吏獄，貶昭州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: Xin, at the beginning of Empress Wu's reign fell into the cruel officials' prison, was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Zhaozhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Empress Wu's reign Xin fell into the cruel officials' prison, was demoted to vice-prefect of Zhaozhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 子嶠，本名餘慶，中興初封嗣濮王。

translations.literal: His son Qiao, original name Yuqing, was at the beginning of the Restoration enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao, originally named Yuqing, was created Heir Prince of Pu at the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，為國子祭酒，同正員。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan he was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Regular Associate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 (724) he was chancellor of the Directorate of Education, regular associate.

sentences.zh: 以王守一妹婿貶邵州別駕，移鄧州別駕，後復其爵。

translations.literal: Because he was son-in-law to Wang Shouyi's younger sister he was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Shaozhou, transferred to Vice-Prefect of Dengzhou, and later his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: As brother-in-law to Wang Shouyi's sister he was demoted to vice-prefect of Shaozhou, moved to Dengzhou, and later had his title restored.

sentences.zh: 庶人祐，太宗第五子也。

translations.literal: Commoner You was Taizong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: You, the commoner, was Taizong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 武德八年，封宜陽王，其年改封楚王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang; that year he was changed to Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 8 (625) he was created Prince of Yiyang; that year his fief was changed to Chu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，徙封燕王，累轉豳州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Prince of Yan and repeatedly transferred as Governor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 (628) he was transferred to Prince of Yan and served repeatedly as governor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封齊王，授齊州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Qi and appointed Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was changed to Prince of Qi and appointed governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 其舅尚乘直長陰弘智謂祐曰：「王兄弟既多，即上百年之後，須得武士自助。」

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Direct Attendant of the Imperial Stud Yin Hongzhi said to You, "Your Highness has many brothers; when the Emperor passes a hundred years you will need warriors to aid yourself."
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Yin Hongzhi, direct attendant of the Imperial Stud, told You, "Your Highness has many brothers; when the Emperor is gone you will need warriors to aid yourself."

sentences.zh: 乃引其妻兄燕弘信謁祐，祐接之甚厚，多賜金帛，令潛募劍士。

translations.literal: He thereupon introduced You's wife's elder brother Yan Hongxin to meet You; You received him very generously, gave much gold and silk, and ordered him secretly to recruit swordsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced You's brother-in-law Yan Hongxin, whom You received generously, lavishing gold and silk and ordering him secretly to recruit swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以子弟成長，慮乖法度，長史、司馬，必取正人。

translations.literal: At first Taizong, because the imperial sons were growing up, feared they would violate law and regulation; Chief Administrators and Directors must be upright men.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taizong, fearing his grown sons would violate law, insisted that chief administrators and directors be upright men.

sentences.zh: 王有虧違，皆遣聞奏。

translations.literal: If a prince had faults or violations, they were all sent to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Any prince's misconduct was to be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 而祐溺情群小，尤好弋獵，長史薛大鼎屢諫不聽，太宗以大鼎輔導無方，竟坐免。

translations.literal: But You indulged petty men and especially loved falconry and hunting; Chief Administrator Xue Dading repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded; Taizong, because Dading's guidance had been ineffective, finally dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: You indulged petty men and loved falconry and hunting. Chief administrator Xue Dading remonstrated repeatedly in vain; Taizong dismissed him for failing to guide the prince.

sentences.zh: 權萬紀前為吳王恪長史，有正直節，以萬紀為祐長史，以匡正之。

translations.literal: Quan Wanji had formerly been Chief Administrator to Prince of Wu Ke and had an upright integrity; Wanji was made You's Chief Administrator to correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wanji, formerly chief administrator to Prince of Wu Ke and a man of integrity, was made You's chief administrator to correct him.

sentences.zh: 萬紀見祐非法，常犯顏切諫。

translations.literal: Wanji saw You's illegal conduct and often offended his countenance with stern remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji saw You's lawlessness and often remonstrated to his face.

sentences.zh: 有昝君謨、梁猛彪者，並以善騎射得幸於祐。

translations.literal: There were Zan Junmo and Liang Mengbiao, both skilled in mounted archery and favored by You.
translations.idiomatic: Zan Junmo and Liang Mengbiao, both skilled in mounted archery, won You's favor.

sentences.zh: 萬紀驟諫不納，遂斥逐之，而祐潛遣招延，狎暱逾甚。

translations.literal: Wanji remonstrated repeatedly without acceptance and thereupon expelled them; yet You secretly sent to summon and draw them in, becoming still more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji remonstrated and then expelled them, but You secretly recalled them and grew still more intimate with them.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮其不能悔過，數以書責讓祐。

translations.literal: Taizong feared he could not repent and several times wrote letters reproaching You.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing You would not repent, Taizong wrote to reproach him several times.

sentences.zh: 萬紀恐並獲罪，謂祐曰：「王，帝之愛子，陛下欲王改悔，故加教訓。

translations.literal: Wanji feared he would also be punished and said to You, "Your Highness is the Emperor's beloved son; the Emperor wishes Your Highness to reform and therefore adds instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji, fearing he too would be punished, told You, "Your Highness is the Emperor's beloved son. He wishes you to reform and therefore instructs you.

sentences.zh: 若能飭躬引過，萬紀請入言之。」

translations.literal: If you can discipline yourself and acknowledge fault, Wanji will go in and speak on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: If you can discipline yourself and acknowledge fault, I will go in and speak for you."

sentences.zh: 祐因附表謝罪。

translations.literal: You thereupon attached a memorial apologizing for fault.
translations.idiomatic: You then submitted a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 萬紀既至，言祐必能改過。

translations.literal: When Wanji arrived he said You would surely be able to reform.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanji reached court he said You would surely reform.

sentences.zh: 太宗意稍解，賜萬紀而諭之，仍以祐前過，敕書誥誡之。

translations.literal: Taizong's mind was somewhat eased; he rewarded Wanji and instructed him, and because of You's former faults issued an edict of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's mind eased somewhat. He rewarded Wanji and instructed him, and because of You's former faults issued an edict of admonition.

sentences.zh: 祐聞萬紀勞勉而獨被責，以為賣己，意甚不平。

translations.literal: When You heard Wanji had been rewarded while he alone was reproached, he thought Wanji had betrayed him and was very resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wanji was rewarded while he alone was reproached, You thought Wanji had betrayed him and grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 萬紀性又褊隘，專以嚴急維持之，城門外不許祐出，所有鷹犬並令解放，又斥出君謨、猛彪，不許與祐相見。

translations.literal: Wanji by nature was also narrow-minded; he relied solely on severity and urgency to control You, not permitting You to go outside the city gate, ordering all hawks and dogs released, and expelling Junmo and Mengbiao, not permitting them to see You.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow by nature, Wanji controlled You by severity alone: no leaving the city gate, all hawks and dogs released, Junmo and Mengbiao expelled and forbidden to see him.

sentences.zh: 祐及君謨以此銜怒，謀殺萬紀。

translations.literal: You together with Junmo therefore harbored anger and plotted to kill Wanji.
translations.idiomatic: You and Junmo therefore nursed anger and plotted to kill Wanji.

sentences.zh: 會事洩，萬紀悉收繫獄，而發驛奏聞。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked, Wanji seized and imprisoned them all and sent express report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked Wanji seized and imprisoned them all and sent express report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔刑部尚書劉德威往按之，並追祐及萬紀入京。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered Minister of Justice Liu Dewei to go investigate, and both You and Wanji were summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 (643) an edict sent Minister of Justice Liu Dewei to investigate; both You and Wanji were summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 祐大懼，俄而萬紀奉詔先行，祐遣燕弘信兄弘亮追於路射殺之。

translations.literal: You was greatly afraid; soon Wanji set out first under edict, and You sent Yan Hongxin's elder brother Hongliang to overtake him on the road and shoot him to death.
translations.idiomatic: You was terrified. When Wanji set out first under edict, You sent Yan Hongxin's brother Hongliang to overtake him on the road and shoot him dead.

sentences.zh: 既殺萬紀，君謨等勸祐起兵，乃召城中男子年十五以上，偽署上柱國、開府儀同三司，開官庫物以行賞。

translations.literal: After killing Wanji, Junmo and the others urged You to raise troops; he thereupon summoned men in the city aged fifteen and above, falsely appointed them Upper Pillar of State and Opening the Government with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, opened the government storehouses to distribute rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Wanji, Junmo and the others urged rebellion. You summoned every man in the city aged fifteen or above, falsely appointed them Upper Pillar of State and Opening the Government with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, and opened the storehouses to pay them.

sentences.zh: 驅百姓入城，繕甲兵。

translations.literal: He drove the common people into the city and repaired armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He drove commoners into the city and readied arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 署官司，其官有拓東王、拓西王之號。

translations.literal: He appointed officials, and among the offices were titles such as Prince Who Expands the East and Prince Who Expands the West.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed officials, including fanciful titles such as Prince Who Expands the East and Prince Who Expands the West.

sentences.zh: 詔遣兵部尚書李勣與劉威便道發兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Minister of War Li Jing and Liu Wei to raise troops by convenient route to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Minister of War Li Jing and Liu Wei to raise troops by the fastest route and attack him.

sentences.zh: 祐每夜引弘亮等五人對妃宴樂，以為得志。

translations.literal: Each night You would summon Hongliang and five others to feast and make music with his consort, thinking himself successful.
translations.idiomatic: Each night You feasted and made music with his consort, summoning Hongliang and five others, thinking himself triumphant.

sentences.zh: 戲笑之隙，語及官軍，弘亮曰：「不須憂也！

translations.literal: In the intervals of jest and laughter, when talk turned to the government army, Hongliang said, "There is no need for worry!
translations.idiomatic: Jesting over wine, when talk turned to the government army, Hongliang said, "No need to worry!

sentences.zh: 右手持酒啖，左手刀拂之。」

translations.literal: In the right hand hold wine and eat; in the left hand let the blade sweep them away."
translations.idiomatic: Wine in the right hand, blade in the left—that is all."

sentences.zh: 祐愛信弘亮，聞之甚樂。

translations.literal: You loved and trusted Hongliang; hearing this he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: You loved and trusted Hongliang and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 太宗手詔祐曰：「吾常誡汝勿近小人，正為此也。

translations.literal: Taizong wrote a personal edict to You, saying, "I often admonished you not to draw near petty men — it was precisely for this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote a personal edict to You: "I often warned you not to draw near petty men—precisely for this.

sentences.zh: 汝素乖誠德，重惑邪言，自延伊禍以取覆滅。

translations.literal: You have long been contrary to sincere virtue and deeply misled by wicked words, yourself inviting this calamity to bring ruin.
translations.idiomatic: You long turned from sincere virtue, believed wicked words, and invited this ruin yourself.

sentences.zh: 痛哉，何愚之甚也！

translations.literal: Alas, how extremely foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how foolish!

sentences.zh: 遂乃為梟為獍，忘孝忘忠，擾亂齊郊，誅夷無罪。

translations.literal: You have become owl and jackal, forgotten filial piety and loyalty, disturbed Qi's borders, and slaughtered the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: You have become owl and jackal, forgotten filial piety and loyalty, disturbed Qi's borders, and slaughtered the innocent.

sentences.zh: 去維城之固，就積薪之危；

translations.literal: You left the solidity of the wall of the realm and approached the peril of a pile of kindling;
translations.idiomatic: You left the realm's solid wall and approached a pile of kindling;

sentences.zh: 壞盤石之親，為尋戈之釁。

translations.literal: you broke the kinship of the foundation stone and made the provocation of raising spears against kin.
translations.idiomatic: you broke foundation-stone kinship and raised spears against your own house.

sentences.zh: 且夫背禮違義，天地所不容；

translations.literal: Moreover to turn your back on ritual and righteousness is what Heaven and Earth cannot contain;
translations.idiomatic: To turn from ritual and righteousness is what Heaven and Earth cannot contain;

sentences.zh: 棄父逃君，人神所共怒。

translations.literal: to abandon father and flee from sovereign is what men and spirits together rage at.
translations.idiomatic: to abandon father and flee sovereign is what men and spirits together rage at.

sentences.zh: 往是吾子，今為國讎。

translations.literal: Yesterday you were my son; today you are the state's enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday you were my son; today you are the state's enemy.

sentences.zh: 萬紀存為忠烈，死不妨義；

translations.literal: Wanji in life was a loyal martyr; in death he does not harm righteousness;
