translations.idiomatic: Wanji in life was a loyal martyr; in death he does not harm righteousness;

sentences.zh: 汝生為賊臣，死為逆鬼。

translations.literal: you in life are a traitor minister; in death you are a rebellious ghost.
translations.idiomatic: you in life are a traitor minister; in death a rebellious ghost.

sentences.zh: 彼則嘉聲不隤，爾則惡跡無窮。

translations.literal: He will have good fame undiminished; you will have evil traces without end.
translations.idiomatic: His good fame will not fall; your evil traces will have no end.

sentences.zh: 吾聞鄭叔、漢戾，並為猖獗，豈期生子，乃自為之？

translations.literal: I have heard that Prince Shu of Zheng and Prince Li of Han both were wildly unruly — who could have expected that in bearing a son one would do it to oneself?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Prince Shu of Zheng and Prince Li of Han were wildly unruly—who expected a father to breed it in his own son?

sentences.zh: 吾所以上慚皇天，下愧后土，嘆惋之甚，知復何云。」

translations.literal: For this I am ashamed before Heaven above and the Earth below; my sighing regret is extreme — what more can I say?"
translations.idiomatic: For this I am ashamed before Heaven and Earth; my grief is beyond words—what more can I say?"

sentences.zh: 太宗題書畢，為之灑泣。

translations.literal: When Taizong finished writing the edict he wept over it.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong finished the edict he wept over it.

sentences.zh: 時李勣等兵未至齊境，而青、淄等數州兵並不從祐之命，祐又傳檄諸縣，亦不從。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing and the others' troops had not yet reached Qi's borders, but the troops of Qing, Zi, and several other prefectures all did not obey You's orders; You also issued proclamations to the counties, and they likewise did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's army had not yet reached Qi, but troops from Qing, Zi, and other prefectures refused You's orders, as did the counties he summoned.

sentences.zh: 或勸祐虜城中子女走入豆子䴚為盜，計未決而兵曹杜行敏謀將執祐，兵士多願從。

translations.literal: Some urged You to seize the city's women and children and flee into Mount Douzi to become bandits; before the plan was decided Military Affairs Officer Du Xingmin plotted to seize You, and many soldiers wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to seize the city's women and children and flee into Mount Douzi as bandits. Before he decided, military affairs officer Du Xingmin plotted to seize him, and many soldiers wished to follow.

sentences.zh: 是夜，乃鑿垣而入，祐與弘亮等五人披甲控弦，入室以自固。

translations.literal: That night they broke through the wall and entered; You together with Hongliang and five others donned armor, drew bows, and entered a room to fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: That night they broke through the wall. You, Hongliang, and five others donned armor, drew bows, and barricaded themselves in a room.

sentences.zh: 行敏列兵圍之，謂祐曰：「昔為帝子，今乃國賊。

translations.literal: Xingmin arrayed troops to surround them and said to You, "Formerly you were the emperor's son; now you are the state's rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmin surrounded them and said to You, "Once you were the emperor's son; now you are the state's rebel.

sentences.zh: 行敏為國討賊，更無所顧，王不速降，當為煨燼。」

translations.literal: Xingmin punishes rebels for the state and has nothing more to consider; if Your Highness does not quickly surrender, you will become ashes."
translations.idiomatic: I punish rebels for the state and have nothing more to consider. If you do not surrender quickly, you will become ashes."

sentences.zh: 命薪草欲積而焚之，祐遂出就擒，餘黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: He ordered firewood and grass piled to burn them; You thereupon came out and was seized, and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered firewood piled to burn them. You came out and was seized; the rest were executed.

sentences.zh: 行敏送祐至京師，賜死於內省，貶為庶人。

translations.literal: Xingmin sent You to the capital; he was granted death in the Inner Quarters and demoted to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmin sent You to the capital. He was granted death in the Inner Quarters and demoted to commoner.

sentences.zh: 國除。

translations.literal: The fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 尋以國公禮葬之。

translations.literal: Soon he was buried with the rites of a duke of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon buried with ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 蜀王愔，太宗第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yin was Taizong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, Prince of Shu, was Taizong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封梁王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was created Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 七年，授襄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633) he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封蜀王，轉益州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Shu and transferred as Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was changed to Prince of Shu and transferred to governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，賜實封八百戶，除岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households and made Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 13 (639) he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households and was made prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 愔常非理毆擊所部縣令，又畋獵無度，數為非法。

translations.literal: Yin often beat the county magistrates under him without reason and hunted without limit, repeatedly acting illegally.
translations.idiomatic: Yin often beat his county magistrates without cause, hunted without limit, and repeatedly broke the law.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒曰：「禽獸調伏，可以馴擾於人；

translations.literal: Taizong angrily said, "Beasts when tamed can be made docile toward men;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said angrily, "Beasts, once tamed, can be made docile toward men;

sentences.zh: 鐵石鐫煉，可為方圓之器。

translations.literal: iron and stone when forged and refined can be made into square and round vessels.
translations.idiomatic: iron and stone, forged and refined, can be shaped into square and round vessels.

sentences.zh: 至如愔者，曾不如禽獸鐵石乎！」

translations.literal: As for one like Yin — is he not even as good as beasts, iron, and stone?"
translations.idiomatic: As for Yin—is he not even as good as beasts, iron, and stone?"

sentences.zh: 乃削封邑及國官之半，貶為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon his fief territory and half his state offices were cut, and he was demoted to Prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His fief and half his state offices were cut, and he was demoted to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.

sentences.zh: 愔在州數遊獵，不避禾稼，深為百姓所怨。

translations.literal: While Yin was in the prefecture he often went hunting and did not avoid the grain crops, deeply resented by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture he hunted repeatedly without avoiding grain crops, deeply resented by the people.

sentences.zh: 典軍楊道整叩馬諫，愔曳而捶之。

translations.literal: Army Controller Yang Daozheng seized the bridle and remonstrated; Yin dragged him down and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Army controller Yang Daozheng seized his bridle and remonstrated; Yin dragged him down and beat him.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，為御史大夫李乾祐所劾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 (650) censor-in-chief Li Qianyou impeached him.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂荊王元景等曰：「先朝櫛風沐雨，平定四方，遠近肅清，車書混一。

translations.literal: Gaozong said to Prince of Jing Yuanjing and others, "The previous reign braved wind and rain, pacified the four quarters, brought distant and near to order, and unified carriage and script.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong told Prince of Jing Yuanjing and others, "The previous reign braved wind and rain, pacified the four quarters, brought order near and far, and unified the realm.

sentences.zh: 上天降禍，奄棄萬邦。

translations.literal: Heaven sent calamity and suddenly abandoned the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent calamity and suddenly took him from the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕纂承洪業，懼均馭朽，與王共戚同憂，為家為國。

translations.literal: I have inherited the great enterprise, fearing I am like one driving rotten wood, sharing sorrow with you princes for family and state.
translations.idiomatic: I have inherited the great enterprise, fearing I drive rotten wood, and share sorrow with you princes for family and state.

sentences.zh: 蜀王畋獵無度，侵擾黎庶，縣令、典軍，無罪被罰。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu hunts without limit, harasses the people, and county magistrates and army controllers are punished though guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu hunts without limit, harasses the people, and punishes guiltless magistrates and army controllers.

sentences.zh: 阿諛即喜，忤意便嗔，如此居官，何以共理百姓？

translations.literal: Flattery pleases him; crossing his will angers him — holding office thus, how can we together govern the people?
translations.idiomatic: Flattery pleases him; crossing his will angers him. How can we govern the people together on such terms?

sentences.zh: 歷觀古來諸王，若能動遵禮度，則慶流子孫；

translations.literal: Looking through the princes of old, if they could act by ritual norms then blessing flowed to sons and grandsons;
translations.idiomatic: Looking through history's princes, those who kept ritual norms blessed their descendants;

sentences.zh: 違越條章，則誅不旋踵。

translations.literal: if they overstepped statutes, execution followed without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: those who overstepped statutes were executed without delay.

sentences.zh: 愔為法司所劾，朕實恥之。」

translations.literal: Yin has been impeached by the law officers; I am truly shamed."
translations.idiomatic: Yin has been impeached by the law officers; I am truly shamed."

sentences.zh: 帝又引楊道整勞勉之，拜為匡道府折衝都尉，賜絹五十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor also summoned Yang Daozheng, comforted and encouraged him, appointed him Commandant of Kuangdao Prefecture, and gave fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also summoned Yang Daozheng, comforted him, appointed him commandant of Kuangdao prefecture, and gave fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 貶愔為黃州刺史。

translations.literal: Yin was demoted to Prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was demoted to prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐與恪謀逆，黜為庶人，徙居巴州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of plotting rebellion with Ke, he was demoted to commoner and moved to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, for plotting rebellion with Ke, he was demoted to commoner and moved to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 尋改為涪陵王。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prince of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon changed to Prince of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Qianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianfeng 2 (667).

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，復其爵土，贈益州大都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰悼。

translations.literal: In the early Xianheng era his title and fief were restored, he was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yizhou, buried with accompaniment at Zhaoling, with posthumous title Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianheng his title and fief were restored. He was posthumously made grand governor of Yizhou, buried at Zhaoling, with posthumous title Dao.

sentences.zh: 封子璠為嗣蜀王，永昌年配流歸誠州而死。

translations.literal: His son Fan was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Shu; in the Yongchang era he was banished to Guicheng and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan was created Heir Prince of Shu; in the Yongchang era he was banished to Guicheng and died there.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以吳王恪孫朗陵王瑋子榆為嗣蜀王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Divine Dragon era, Ke's grandson Prince of Langling Wei and his son Yu were made to succeed as Heir Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Dragon Restoration Ke's grandson Wei, Prince of Langling, and his son Yu were made to succeed as heir prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 蔣王惲，太宗第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang Yun was Taizong's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Jiang, was Taizong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封郯王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was created Prince of Tan.

sentences.zh: 八年，授洺州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 8 (634) he was appointed prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封蔣王、安州都督，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Jiang and Governor of Anzhou, granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was changed to Prince of Jiang and governor of Anzhou, with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，除梁州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he was made Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 3 (652) he was made governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 惲在安州，多造器用服玩，及將行，有遞車四百兩。

translations.literal: While Yun was in Anzhou he made many utensils, robes, and playthings; when he was about to depart there were four hundred relay carriages.
translations.idiomatic: While in Anzhou Yun made many utensils, robes, and playthings; when he departed there were four hundred relay carriages.

sentences.zh: 州縣不堪其勞，為有司所劾，帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The prefecture and counties could not bear the labor and were impeached by the responsible officials; the emperor especially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture and counties could not bear the labor and officials impeached him; the emperor especially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 後歷遂、相二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Prefect of Sui and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as prefect of Sui and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 上元年，有人詣闕誣告惲謀反，惶懼自殺，贈司空、荊州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan someone went to the palace gate to falsely accuse Yun of plotting rebellion; in fear he killed himself and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Grand Governor of Jingzhou, buried with accompaniment at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1 (674) someone falsely accused Yun of plotting rebellion at the palace gate. In fear he killed himself and was posthumously made Minister of Works and grand governor of Jingzhou, buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子煒嗣，歷沂州刺史，垂拱中為則天所害。

translations.literal: His son Wei succeeded, served as Prefect of Yi, and in the Chuigong era was killed by Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei succeeded, served as prefect of Yi, and in the Chuigong era was killed by Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 子銑，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xian died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian died young.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，封銑子紹宗為嗣蔣王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Divine Dragon era Xian's son Shaozong was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Dragon Restoration Xian's son Shaozong was created Heir Prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 2 (708) he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為太子家令同正員卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Regular Associate Master of the Crown Prince's Household and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he served as regular associate master of the crown prince's household and died.

sentences.zh: 子欽福嗣，為率更令，同正員。

translations.literal: His son Qinfu succeeded and was Director of the Imperial Observatory, Regular Associate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinfu succeeded as director of the Imperial Observatory, regular associate.

sentences.zh: 天寶初削官，於錦州安置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao his office was cut and he was settled at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao his office was cut and he was settled at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二載，為南郡長史同正。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was Regular Associate Chief Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 12 (753) he was regular associate chief administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 惲子煌，蔡國公。

translations.literal: Yun's son Huang was Duke of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Huang was Duke of Cai.

sentences.zh: 煌孫之芳，幼有令譽，頗善五言詩，宗室推之。

translations.literal: Huang's grandson Zhifang from youth had a fine reputation, was quite skilled in five-character poetry, and was esteemed among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's grandson Zhifang had a fine reputation from youth, was skilled in five-character poetry, and was esteemed in the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 開元末為駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he was Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyuan he was vice director of the Imperial Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，安祿山奏為范陽司馬。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao An Lushan memorialized appointing him Secretary of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 (754) An Lushan memorialized appointing him secretary of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 及祿山起逆，自拔歸西京，授右司郎中，歷工部侍郎、太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Lushan rose in rebellion he freed himself and returned to the Western Capital, was appointed Vice Director of the Right Department, and successively served as Vice Minister of Works and Right Vice Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he escaped to the Western Capital, was appointed vice director of the Right Department, and served successively as vice minister of Works and right vice mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，兵革未清，吐蕃又犯邊，侵軼原、會。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde the warfare was not yet settled and Tibet again invaded the border, raiding Yuan and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1 (763) warfare was not yet settled and Tibet again invaded, raiding Yuan and Hui.

sentences.zh: 乃遣之芳兼御史大夫，使吐蕃，被留境上，二年而歸。

translations.literal: Zhifang was sent as Concurrent Censor-in-Chief as envoy to Tibet, was detained on the border, and returned after two years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang was sent as acting censor-in-chief to Tibet, was detained on the border, and returned after two years.

sentences.zh: 除禮部尚書，尋改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was made Minister of Rites and soon changed to Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites and soon changed to mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 惲子休道。

translations.literal: Yun's son Xiudao.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son was Xiudao.

sentences.zh: 道子琚，本名思順。

translations.literal: Xiudao's son Ju, original name Sishun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiudao's son Ju was originally named Sishun.

sentences.zh: 中興封嗣趙王，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the Restoration he was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Zhao and made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration he was created Heir Prince of Zhao and made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，改封中山郡王，右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan he was changed to Prince of Zhongshan commandery and General of the Right Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 (724) he was changed to Prince of Zhongshan commandery and general of the Right Garrison.

sentences.zh: 越王貞，太宗第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Zhen was Taizong's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Prince of Yue, was Taizong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封漢王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was created Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 七年，授徐州都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633) he was appointed governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封原王，尋徙封越王，拜揚州都督，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Yuan, soon transferred to Prince of Yue, appointed Governor of Yangzhou, and granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was changed to Prince of Yuan, soon to Prince of Yue, named governor of Yangzhou, with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十七年，轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred as Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 (643) he was transferred to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，授安州都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was appointed Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 4 (653) he was appointed governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，復轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he was again transferred as Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era he was again transferred to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞少善騎射，頗涉文史，兼有吏干。

translations.literal: Zhen from youth was skilled in mounted archery, was quite versed in literature and history, and also had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhen was skilled in mounted archery, versed in literature and history, and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 所在或偏受讒言，官僚有正直者多被貶退，又縱諸僮豎侵暴部人，由是人伏其才而鄙其行。

translations.literal: Wherever he was he sometimes partially accepted slanderous words; upright officials were mostly demoted and dismissed, and he also allowed his pages and servants to bully the people under him; therefore people respected his talent yet despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he sometimes heeded slander; upright officials were demoted and his pages bullied the people—men respected his talent yet despised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，加太子太傅，除蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court she added Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and made him Prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held court she added Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and made him prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 自則天稱制，貞與韓王元嘉、魯王靈夔、霍王元軌及元嘉子黃國公譔、靈夔子范陽王藹、元軌子江都王緒並貞長子博州刺史琅邪王沖等，密有匡復之志。

translations.literal: From the time Empress Wu assumed the regnal title, Zhen together with Prince of Han Yuanjia, Prince of Lu Lingqian, Prince of Huo Yuanji, Yuanjia's son Duke of Huangguo Shen, Lingqian's son Prince of Fanyang Ai, Yuanji's son Prince of Jiangdu Xu, and Zhen's eldest son Chong, Prefect of Bo and Prince of Langye, secretly had the will to restore the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu assumed power, Zhen joined Prince of Han Yuanjia, Prince of Lu Lingqian, Prince of Huo Yuanji, Yuanjia's son Shen Duke of Huangguo, Lingqian's son Ai Prince of Fanyang, Yuanji's son Xu Prince of Jiangdu, and Zhen's eldest son Chong, Langye prince and Bo prefect, in a secret plan to restore the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年七月，譔作謬書與貞云：「內人病漸重，恐須早療；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Chuigong, Shen composed a false letter to Zhen saying, "The inner person is gradually gravely ill and probably needs early treatment;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chuigong 3 (687) Shen forged a letter to Zhen: "The inner person grows gravely ill and needs early treatment;

sentences.zh: 若至今冬，恐成痼疾，宜早下手，仍速相報。」

translations.literal: if it waits until this winter it will probably become a chronic ailment — you should act early and report back quickly."
translations.idiomatic: if you wait until winter it may become incurable. Act early and report back quickly."

sentences.zh: 是歲，則天以明堂成，將行大享之禮，追皇宗赴集。

translations.literal: That year, because Empress Wu had completed the Bright Hall and was about to perform the great suburban sacrifice, she summoned the imperial clansmen to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: That year Empress Wu completed the Bright Hall and was about to perform the great suburban sacrifice, summoning the imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉因遞相語云：「大享之際，神皇必遣人告諸王密，因大行誅戮，皇家子弟無遺種矣。」

translations.literal: Yuanjia therefore sent word to one another, saying, "At the time of the great sacrifice the Divine Sovereign will surely send people to accuse the princes in secret and carry out a great slaughter — none of the imperial sons and grandsons will be left."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia sent word among them: "At the great sacrifice the empress will surely accuse the princes in secret and slaughter them—no imperial descendant will be left."

sentences.zh: 譔遂詐為皇帝璽書與沖云：「朕被幽縶，王等宜各救拔我也。」

translations.literal: Shen thereupon forged an imperial seal letter to Chong saying, "I am held in secret imprisonment; you princes should each rescue me."
translations.idiomatic: Shen forged an imperial letter to Chong: "I am held in secret imprisonment; you princes must rescue me."

sentences.zh: 沖在博州，又偽為皇帝璽書云：「神皇欲傾李家之社稷，移國祚於武氏。」

translations.literal: Chong, in Bo, also forged an imperial seal letter saying, "The Divine Sovereign wishes to overturn the Li family's altars of soil and grain and shift the mandate of state to the Wu clan."
translations.idiomatic: Chong in Bo also forged an imperial letter: "The empress wishes to overturn the Li altars and shift the mandate to the Wu clan."

sentences.zh: 遂命長史蕭德琮等召募士卒，分報韓、魯、霍、越、紀等五王，各令起兵應接，以赴神都。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Chief Administrator Xiao Decong and others to recruit soldiers, separately report to the five princes Han, Lu, Huo, Yue, and Ji to each raise troops in response and march to the Divine Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered chief administrator Xiao Decong and others to recruit troops and summon the five princes of Han, Lu, Huo, Yue, and Ji to raise forces and march on the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 初，沖與諸王連謀，及沖先發而莫有應者，惟貞以父子之故，獨舉兵以應之。

translations.literal: At first Chong had conspired with the princes, but when Chong rose first and none responded, only Zhen because of the father-son bond alone raised troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had conspired with the princes, but when he rose first none responded—only Zhen, bound by father and son, raised troops alone.

sentences.zh: 尋遣兵破上蔡縣，聞沖敗，恐懼，索鎖欲自拘馳驛詣闕謝罪。

translations.literal: Soon he sent troops to capture Shangcai county; hearing Chong was defeated, he was afraid, sought chains, and intended to bind himself and rush by post to the palace to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to capture Shangcai county; hearing Chong was defeated he sought chains and prepared to bind himself and rush to confess.

sentences.zh: 會其所署新蔡令傅延慶得勇士二千餘人，貞遂有拒敵之意。

translations.literal: As it happened the new magistrate of Shangcai he had appointed, Fu Yanqing, obtained more than two thousand stalwart men, and Zhen thereupon had the will to resist.
translations.idiomatic: His appointed new magistrate of Shangcai, Fu Yanqing, raised more than two thousand stalwarts, and Zhen found the will to resist.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言於其眾曰：「琅邪王已破魏、相數州，聚兵至二十萬，朝夕即到，爾宜勉之。」

translations.literal: He thereupon proclaimed to his host, "Prince of Langye has already broken Wei and several other prefectures, gathered troops to two hundred thousand, and will arrive within the day — you should exert yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed to his host, "Prince of Langye has already broken Wei and several prefectures, gathered two hundred thousand men, and will arrive within the day. Exert yourselves."

sentences.zh: 征屬縣兵至七千人，分為五營。

translations.literal: He summoned county troops to seven thousand men and divided them into five camps.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned seven thousand county troops and divided them into five camps.

sentences.zh: 貞自為中營，署其所親汝陽縣丞裴守德為大將軍、內營總管；

translations.literal: Zhen himself took the central camp and appointed his close associate Vice-Magistrate of Ruyang Pei Shoude as Grand General and Commander of the Inner Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen took the central camp and appointed his close associate Pei Shoude, vice-magistrate of Ruyang, grand general and commander of the inner camp;

sentences.zh: 趙成美為左中郎將，押左營；

translations.literal: Zhao Chengmei as Left Central Commandant commanding the Left Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chengmei as left central commandant commanding the left camp;

sentences.zh: 閭弘道為右中郎將，押右營；

translations.literal: Lu Hongdao as Right Central Commandant commanding the Right Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongdao as right central commandant commanding the right camp;

sentences.zh: 安摩訶為郎將、後軍總管；

translations.literal: An Mohe as Commandant and Commander of the Rear Army;
translations.idiomatic: An Mohe as commandant and commander of the rear army;

sentences.zh: 王孝志為右將軍、前軍總管。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaozhi as Right General and Commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaozhi as right general and commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又以蔡州長史韋慶禮為銀青光祿大夫，行其府司馬。

translations.literal: He also made Chief Administrator of Cai Wei Qingli Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace and Acting Mansion Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Cai chief administrator Wei Qingli Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace and acting mansion secretary.

sentences.zh: 凡署九品已上官五百餘人。

translations.literal: In all he appointed more than five hundred officials of the ninth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: In all he appointed more than five hundred officials of the ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 令道士及僧轉讀諸經，以祈事集，家僮、戰士咸帶符以辟兵。

translations.literal: He ordered Daoist priests and Buddhist monks to recite scriptures to pray for success; household slaves and warriors all wore talismans to ward off weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Daoist priests and Buddhist monks to recite scriptures for success; household slaves and warriors wore talismans to ward off weapons.

sentences.zh: 其所署官皆迫脅見從，本無鬥志，惟裴守德實與之同。

translations.literal: The officials he appointed were all compelled to follow and had no fighting will from the start; only Pei Shoude was truly of one mind with him.
translations.idiomatic: His appointed officials were all compelled followers without fighting will; only Pei Shoude was truly with him.

sentences.zh: 守德驍勇，善騎射，貞將起事，便以女良鄉縣主妻之，而委以爪牙心腹之任。

translations.literal: Shoude was fierce and brave, skilled in mounted archery; when Zhen was about to rise he gave him his daughter the Princess of Liangxiang in marriage and entrusted him with the role of trusted henchman.
translations.idiomatic: Shoude was fierce, brave, and skilled in mounted archery. When Zhen rose he gave him his daughter, Princess of Liangxiang, in marriage and trusted him as henchman.

sentences.zh: 則天命左豹韜衛大將軍麹崇裕為中軍大總管，夏官尚書岑長倩為後軍大總管，率兵十萬討之，仍令鳳閣侍郎張光輔為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Left Leopard-Tawny Guard Grand General Qu Chongyu as Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army, Minister of Summer Works Cen Changqian as Commander-in-Chief of the Rear Army, to lead a hundred thousand troops to attack him, and still ordered Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Zhang Guangfu as Commander over the Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered Left Leopard-Tawny Guard grand general Qu Chongyu as central army commander-in-chief and Minister of Summer Works Cen Changqian as rear army commander-in-chief with a hundred thousand troops, with Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Zhang Guangfu as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 於是制削貞及沖屬籍，改姓虺氏。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict stripped Zhen and Chong from the register and changed their surname to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Zhen and Chong from the imperial register and changed their surname to Hui.

sentences.zh: 崇裕等軍至蔡州城東四十里，貞命少子規及裴守德拒戰。

translations.literal: When Chongyu and the others' army reached forty li east of Cai prefecture's city, Zhen ordered his youngest son Gui and Pei Shoude to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyu's army reached forty li east of Cai city, Zhen ordered his youngest son Gui and Pei Shoude to resist.

sentences.zh: 規等兵潰而歸，貞大懼，閉門自守。

translations.literal: Gui and the others' troops collapsed and returned; Zhen was greatly afraid, closed the gates, and held himself inside.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's troops collapsed and fled back. Zhen was terrified, closed the gates, and held inside.

sentences.zh: 裴守德排閣入，問王安在，意欲殺貞以自購也。

translations.literal: Pei Shoude pushed open the side door and entered, asking where the prince was, intending to kill Zhen to buy himself off.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shoude pushed open a side door, asking where the prince was, intending to kill Zhen to buy himself off.

sentences.zh: 官軍進逼州城，貞家僮悉力衛，貞曰：「事即如此，豈得受戮辱，當須自為計。」

translations.literal: As the government army pressed the prefectural city, Zhen's household slaves all exerted themselves in defense; Zhen said, "Matters have come to this — how can one accept disgrace in slaughter? One must make one's own plan."
translations.idiomatic: As the government army pressed the city, Zhen's household slaves fought hard. Zhen said, "Matters have come to this—how accept slaughter in disgrace? I must make my own plan."

sentences.zh: 貞乃飲藥而死。

translations.literal: Zhen thereupon drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 家僮方始一時散，舍仗就擒。

translations.literal: The household slaves only then scattered at once, laying aside weapons and submitting to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the household slaves scatter, lay down arms, and submit to capture.

sentences.zh: 規亦縊其母自殺，守德攜良鄉縣主亦同縊於別所。

translations.literal: Gui also hanged his mother and killed herself; Shoude took the Princess of Liangxiang and likewise hanged themselves in another place.
translations.idiomatic: Gui hanged his mother and killed himself; Shoude took Princess of Liangxiang and hanged themselves elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 麹崇裕斬貞父子及裴守德等，傳首東都，梟於闕下。

translations.literal: Qu Chongyu beheaded Zhen, father and sons, and Pei Shoude and the rest, sent the heads to the Eastern Capital, and displayed them below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Chongyu beheaded Zhen, his sons, Pei Shoude, and the rest, sent the heads to the Eastern Capital, and displayed them below the gate.

sentences.zh: 貞起兵凡二十日而敗。

translations.literal: Zhen's rising of troops lasted only twenty days before defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's rising lasted only twenty days before defeat.

sentences.zh: 貞之在蔡州，數奏免所部租賦以結人心，家僮千人，馬數千匹，外托以畋獵，內實習武備。

translations.literal: While Zhen was in Cai he several times memorialized to exempt his jurisdiction's rent and tax to win hearts; he had a thousand household slaves and several thousand horses, outwardly claiming hunting while inwardly actually drilling arms.
translations.idiomatic: In Cai he repeatedly memorialized to exempt rent and tax to win hearts. He kept a thousand household slaves and several thousand horses, outwardly hunting while inwardly drilling arms.

sentences.zh: 嘗游於城西水門橋，臨水自鑑，不見其首，心甚惡之，未幾而及禍。

translations.literal: He once toured west of the city at the Water Gate Bridge; gazing into the water to see himself, he did not see his head and greatly hated it; before long calamity arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Once touring west of the city at Water Gate Bridge he gazed into the water and did not see his head—a omen he hated. Soon calamity came.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復爵土，與子沖俱復舊姓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Divine Dragon era his title and fief were posthumously restored, and he together with his son Chong resumed their original surnames.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Dragon Restoration his title and fief were posthumously restored, and he and Chong resumed their original surnames.

sentences.zh: 初，貞將起兵，作書與壽州刺史、駙馬都尉趙瑰曰：「佇總義兵，來入貴境。」

translations.literal: At first, when Zhen was about to raise troops, he wrote to Shou Prefect and Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law's Residence Zhao Gui, saying, "I await gathering the righteous army to enter your honored territory."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was about to rise he wrote to Shou prefect and imperial son-in-law Zhao Gui: "I await gathering the righteous army to enter your territory."

sentences.zh: 瑰甚喜，復許率兵相應。

translations.literal: Gui was very pleased and again promised to lead troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was pleased and again promised to lead troops in response.

sentences.zh: 瑰妻常樂長公主，高祖第七女，和思皇后之母也，謂其使曰：「為我報越王，與其進不與其退。

translations.literal: Gui's wife was Princess Chang Le, the seventh daughter of Gaozu and mother of Empress Hesiji; she said to the envoy, "Report to Prince of Yue for me: go forward with him, not back with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's wife was Princess Chang Le, Gaozu's seventh daughter and mother of Empress Hesiji. She told the envoy, "Report to Prince of Yue for me: go forward with him, not back with him.

sentences.zh: 爾諸王若是男兒，不應至許時尚未舉動。

translations.literal: You princes, if you are men, should not by this time still not have acted.
translations.idiomatic: You princes, if you are men, should not by now still have failed to act.

sentences.zh: 我常見耆老雲，隋文帝將篡奪周室，尉遲迥是周家外甥，猶能起兵相州，連結突厥，天下聞風，莫不響應。

translations.literal: I often hear elders say that when Emperor Wen of Sui was about to usurp the Zhou house, Yuwen Jiong as maternal nephew of the Zhou house still could raise troops at Xiangzhou, link with the Turks, and make the realm respond to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: I often hear elders say that when Emperor Wen of Sui was about to usurp Zhou, Yuwen Jiong, Zhou's maternal nephew, still raised troops at Xiangzhou, linked with the Turks, and made the realm respond.

sentences.zh: 況爾諸王，並國家懿親，宗社是托，豈不學尉遲迥感恩效節，捨生取義耶？

translations.literal: How much more you princes, all honored kin of the state with the altars entrusted to you — will you not learn from Yuwen Jiong's gratitude and loyal service, giving life and taking righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: How much more you princes—all honored kin with the altars entrusted to you—will you not learn from Yuwen Jiong's loyal service and give life for righteousness?

sentences.zh: 夫為臣子，若救國家則為忠，不救則為逆。

translations.literal: As ministers and sons, to save the state is loyalty; not to save is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: As ministers and sons, to save the state is loyalty; not to save is rebellion.

sentences.zh: 諸王必須以匡救為急，不可虛生浪死，取笑於後代。」

translations.literal: You princes must take restoration as urgent and cannot die in vain to become a laughingstock for later generations."
translations.idiomatic: You princes must take restoration as urgent and cannot die in vain to become a laughingstock for later generations."

sentences.zh: 及貞等敗，瑰與公主亦伏誅。

translations.literal: When Zhen and the others were defeated, Gui and the princess also were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen and the others were defeated, Gui and the princess were also executed.

sentences.zh: 沖，貞長子也。

translations.literal: Chong was Zhen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was Zhen's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 好文學，善騎射、歷密、濟、博三州刺史，皆有能名。

translations.literal: He loved literature, was skilled in mounted archery, and successively served as Prefect of Mi, Ji, and Bo, all with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature, was skilled in mounted archery, and served successively as prefect of Mi, Ji, and Bo, all with reputations for ability.

sentences.zh: 初，沖自博州募得五千餘人，欲渡河攻濟州，先取武水縣。

translations.literal: At first Chong recruited more than five thousand men at Bo and intended to cross the river to attack Jizhou, first taking Wushui county.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chong recruited more than five thousand men at Bo and intended to cross the river to attack Jizhou, first taking Wushui county.

sentences.zh: 縣令郭務悌赴魏州請援，魏州莘縣令馬玄素領兵千七百人邀之於路，恐力不敵，先入武水城，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Magistrate Guo Wuti of the county went to Weizhou to request aid; Magistrate Ma Xuansu of Shen county in Weizhou led one thousand seven hundred troops to intercept on the road, fearing insufficient strength, first entered Wushui city and closed the gates to resist.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrate Guo Wuti went to Weizhou for aid. Shen county magistrate Ma Xuansu in Weizhou led seventeen hundred troops to intercept, fearing insufficient strength, entered Wushui first, and closed the gates.

sentences.zh: 沖乃令積草車上，放火燒南門，擬乘火突入。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon ordered hay piled on carts, set fire to burn the south gate, intending to burst in amid the flames.
translations.idiomatic: Chong piled hay on carts, set fire to the south gate, and intended to burst in amid the flames.

sentences.zh: 火之未起，南風甚急，及火已燃，遽回為北風，未至城門，燒草已甚，衝軍由是沮氣。

translations.literal: Before the fire rose the south wind was very strong; when the fire had burned it suddenly turned to north wind; before reaching the city gate the hay was already greatly burned, and Chong's army thereby lost spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fire rose a strong south wind blew; when it burned the wind suddenly turned north. Before reaching the gate the hay was consumed, and Chong's army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 有堂邑丞董玄寂為沖統帥兵仗，及衝擊武水，玄寂曰：「琅邪王與國家交戰，此乃反也。」

translations.literal: There was Assistant Magistrate of Tangyi Dong Xuanji commanding Chong's weapons; when Chong attacked Wushui, Xuanji said, "Prince of Langye is fighting the state — this is rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Tangyi assistant magistrate Dong Xuanji commanded Chong's weapons. When Chong attacked Wushui, Xuanji said, "Prince of Langye is fighting the state—this is rebellion."

sentences.zh: 沖聞之，斬玄寂以徇。

translations.literal: When Chong heard it he beheaded Xuanji to display.
translations.idiomatic: Chong beheaded Xuanji and displayed the head.

sentences.zh: 兵眾懼而散入草澤，不可禁止，惟有家僮左右不過數十而已。

translations.literal: The soldiers feared and scattered into marshes and wilds and could not be stopped; there remained only household slaves and attendants, no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers feared and scattered into marshes; only several tens of household slaves and attendants remained.

sentences.zh: 乃卻走入博州城，為守門者所殺。

translations.literal: He thereupon turned back and entered Bo prefecture's city and was killed by the gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back into Bo city and was killed by the gate guards.

sentences.zh: 則天命左金吾將軍丘神勣為清平道行軍大總管以討沖，兵未至，沖已死，傳首東都，梟於闕下。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Left Golden Guard General Qiu Shenji as Commander-in-Chief of the Qingping Circuit Field Army to attack Chong; the troops had not arrived when Chong was already dead; his head was sent to the Eastern Capital and displayed below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered Left Golden Guard general Qiu Shenji as commander-in-chief of the Qingping circuit to attack Chong. Before the troops arrived Chong was dead; his head was sent to the Eastern Capital and displayed below the gate.

sentences.zh: 衝起兵凡七日而敗。

translations.literal: Chong's rising of troops lasted only seven days before defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's rising lasted only seven days before defeat.

sentences.zh: 沖三弟：倩，封常山公，歷常州別駕，坐與父兄連謀伏誅。

translations.literal: Chong had three younger brothers: Qian, enfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan, served as Vice-Prefect of Changzhou, and was executed for conspiring with father and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had three younger brothers. Qian, Duke of Hengshan and vice-prefect of Changzhou, was executed for conspiring with his father and brothers.

sentences.zh: 溫，以告其朋黨得實，減死流嶺南，尋卒。

translations.literal: Wen, because he reported his faction and the facts were verified, had death reduced to banishment to Lingnan, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, because he reported his faction with verified facts, had death reduced to banishment to Lingnan and soon died.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，侍中敬暉等以沖父子翼戴皇家，義存社稷，請復其官爵，武三思令昭容上官氏代中宗手詔不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Divine Dragon era Attendant-in-Ordinary Jing Hui and others, because Chong father and son had supported the imperial house and preserved the altars of soil and grain, requested restoration of their offices and titles; Wu San Si had Lady Shangguan of Zhaorong substitute for Zhongzong's personal edict refusing.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Dragon Restoration attendant-in-ordinary Jing Hui and others, because Chong father and son had supported the imperial house, requested restoration of their offices and titles; Wu San Si had Lady Shangguan of Zhaorong substitute for Zhongzong's personal edict refusing.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，詔追復爵土，令備禮改葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan an edict posthumously restored title and fief and ordered full rites for reburial.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 4 (716) an edict posthumously restored title and fief and ordered full rites for reburial.

sentences.zh: 太常奏謚議曰：「故越王貞，往者願匡宗社，夙懷誅呂之謀；

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies submitted the posthumous discussion, saying, "The late Prince of Yue Zhen, in former days wished to restore the imperial altars and long harbored the plan to execute the Lü clan;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies submitted the posthumous discussion: "The late Prince of Yue Zhen once wished to restore the imperial altars and long harbored the plan to execute the Lü clan;

sentences.zh: 乃心王國，用擊非劉之議。

translations.literal: his heart was set on the royal house and he employed the argument to strike down the non-Liu.
translations.idiomatic: his heart was set on the royal house and he struck at the non-Liu.

sentences.zh: 以茲獲戾，上悼聖心。

translations.literal: For this he incurred guilt and the sage heart mourned.
translations.idiomatic: For this he incurred guilt and the sage heart mourned.

sentences.zh: 謹按謚法『死不忘君曰敬』，請謚曰敬。」

translations.literal: According to the posthumous norms, 'dying without forgetting the sovereign is called Jing' — I request the posthumous title Jing."
translations.idiomatic: According to the posthumous norms, 'dying without forgetting the sovereign is called Jing'—I request the posthumous title Jing."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was accepted.

sentences.zh: 五年，下詔曰：「九族以親，克敦其教；

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict was issued, saying, "The nine clans through kinship fulfill their teaching;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict said, "The nine clans through kinship fulfill their teaching;

sentences.zh: 百代必祀，允竟厥德。

translations.literal: a hundred generations must sacrifice — fully completing their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: a hundred generations must sacrifice—fully completing their virtue.

sentences.zh: 故蔡州刺史、越王貞，執心不回，臨事能斷。

translations.literal: Therefore the former Prefect of Cai, Prince of Yue Zhen, held his will unbending and in affairs could decide.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former Cai prefect, Prince of Yue Zhen, held his will unbending and could decide in affairs.

sentences.zh: 粵自籓國，勤於王家。

translations.literal: From his territorial state he diligently served the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: From his territorial state he diligently served the royal house.

sentences.zh: 弘道之後，寶圖將缺，懷劉章之輔漢，追鄭武之翊周。

translations.literal: After the broad way, the precious chart was about to lack; he cherished Liu Zhang's aid to Han and pursued Zheng Wu's support of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the broad way the precious chart was about to fail; he cherished Liu Zhang's aid to Han and pursued Zheng Wu's support of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 遂能奮不顧身，率先唱義。

translations.literal: Thereupon he could rouse himself without regard for body and take the lead in proclaiming righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he roused himself without regard for body and took the lead in proclaiming righteousness.

sentences.zh: 雖英謀未克，而忠節居多。

translations.literal: Though heroic planning did not succeed, loyal integrity predominated.
translations.idiomatic: Though heroic planning did not succeed, loyal integrity predominated.

sentences.zh: 嗣絕國除，年逾二紀，奠享淪廢，甚為憫焉。

translations.literal: The succession cut off and the state abolished, more than twenty years passed; sacrifices fell into ruin — it is greatly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The succession was cut off and the state abolished for more than twenty years; sacrifices fell into ruin—greatly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 永言興繼，式備典冊。

translations.literal: Words of raising and continuing — prepare the canonical records.
translations.idiomatic: Words of raising and continuing—prepare the canonical records.

sentences.zh: 其封貞侄孫故許王男左監門衛將軍、夔國公琳為嗣越王，以奉其祀。

translations.literal: Enfeoff Zhen's nephew's son, the former Prince of Xu, the man's son Left Gate Guard General Duke of Kui Lin, as Heir Prince of Yue to attend his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoff Zhen's nephew's son, the former Prince of Xu's son, Left Gate Guard general Duke of Kui Lin, as Heir Prince of Yue to attend his sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 仍官為立碑。」

translations.literal: Still order an office to erect a stele."
translations.idiomatic: Still order an office to erect a stele."

sentences.zh: 琳尋卒，國除。

translations.literal: Lin soon died and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Lin soon died and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 紀王慎，太宗第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Shen was Taizong's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Prince of Ji, was Taizong's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，封申王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was created Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 七年，授秦州都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633) he was appointed governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封紀王，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Prince of Ji and granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 (636) he was changed to Prince of Ji with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷襄州刺史，以善政聞，璽書勞勉，百姓為之立碑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred as Prefect of Xiangzhou; he was known for good government, received imperial writing of comfort and encouragement, and the common people erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 (643) he was transferred to prefect of Xiangzhou, was known for good government, received imperial commendation, and the people erected a stele for him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加實封滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) his substantive fief was increased to a full thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 (650) he was appointed grand general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，授荊州都督，累除刑州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Governor of Jingzhou and repeatedly removed as Prefect of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 (651) he was appointed governor of Jingzhou and later served repeatedly as prefect of Xing.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，加授太子太師，轉貝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming he was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and transferred as Prefect of Bei.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenming 1 (684) he was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and transferred to prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 慎少好學，長於文史，皇族中與越王貞齊名，時人號為紀、越。

translations.literal: Shen from youth loved learning, excelled in literature and history, and among the imperial clan was famed equally with Prince of Yue Zhen; people of the time called them Ji and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shen loved learning and excelled in literature and history; in the imperial clan he was famed equally with Prince of Yue Zhen—men called them Ji and Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，貞將起事，慎不肯同謀；

translations.literal: At first, when Zhen was about to rise, Shen would not join the plot;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was about to rise Shen would not join the plot;

sentences.zh: 及貞敗，慎亦下獄。

translations.literal: when Zhen was defeated, Shen also was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhen was defeated Shen was also imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 臨刑放免，改姓虺氏，仍載以檻車，配流嶺表，道至蒲州而卒。

translations.literal: At the time of execution he was released, his surname changed to Hui, and he was still loaded in a caged cart and banished to Lingnan; on the road he died at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At execution he was released, his surname changed to Hui, loaded in a caged cart and banished to Lingnan; he died on the road at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 慎長子和州刺史東平王續最知名，早卒。

translations.literal: Shen's eldest son Xu, Prefect of He and Prince of Dongping, was most renowned and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's eldest son Xu, He prefect and Prince of Dongping, was most renowned and died young.

sentences.zh: 次子沂州刺史義陽王琮、楚國公睿、遂州別駕襄郡公秀、廣化郡公獻、建平郡公欽等五人，垂拱中並遇害，家屬徙嶺南。

translations.literal: The second son Cong, Prefect of Yi and Prince of Yiyang; the third son Rui, Duke of Chu; the fourth son Xiu, Duke of Xiang; the fifth son Xian, Duke of Guanghua; the sixth son Qin, Duke of Jianping — all five in the Chuigong era met with harm and their families were moved to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Cong, Yi prefect and Prince of Yiyang; third son Rui, Duke of Chu; fourth son Xiu, Duke of Xiang; fifth son Xian, Duke of Guanghua; sixth son Qin, Duke of Jianping—all five were killed in the Chuigong era and their families moved to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 中興初，追復官爵，令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration offices and titles were posthumously restored and reburial with rites was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration offices and titles were posthumously restored and reburial with rites was ordered.

sentences.zh: 封慎少子鐵誠為嗣紀王，後改名澄。

translations.literal: Shen's youngest son Tiechen was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Ji and later changed his name to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's youngest son Tiechen was created Heir Prince of Ji and later changed his name to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) he was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 開元初，歷德、瀛、冀三州刺史、左驍衛將軍，薨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he successively served as Prefect of De, Ying, and Ji and General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he served successively as prefect of De, Ying, and Ji and general of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and died.

sentences.zh: 子行同嗣，天寶中為右贊善大夫，同正員。

translations.literal: His son Xingtong succeeded and in the Tianbao era was Right Mentor, Regular Associate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingtong succeeded and in the Tianbao era was right mentor, regular associate.

sentences.zh: 江王囂，太宗第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang Xiao was Taizong's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, Prince of Jiang, was Taizong's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年受封，六年薨，謚曰殤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment; in the sixth year he died, with posthumous title Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was enfeoffed; in Zhenguan 6 (632) he died, with posthumous title Shang.

sentences.zh: 代王簡，太宗第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Dai Jian was Taizong's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Prince of Dai, was Taizong's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年受封，其年薨，無後，國除。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment; that year he died, having no heir; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 (631) he was enfeoffed; that year he died without heir and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 趙王福，太宗第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Fu was Taizong's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, Prince of Zhao, was Taizong's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年受封，出後隱太子建成。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment and was given in adoption to succeed the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 13 (639) he was enfeoffed and adopted to succeed the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授秦州都督，賜實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Governor of Qinzhou and granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 18 (644) he was appointed governor of Qinzhou with a substantive fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加右衛大將軍，累授梁州都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was added as Grand General of the Right Guard and repeatedly appointed Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) he was added as grand general of the Right Guard and repeatedly appointed governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年薨，贈司空、并州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xianheng and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Governor of Bingzhou, buried with accompaniment at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianheng 1 (670) and was posthumously made Minister of Works and governor of Bingzhou, buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 中興初，封蔣王惲孫思順為嗣趙王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration Prince of Jiang Yun's grandson Sishun was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration Yun Prince of Jiang's grandson Sishun was created Heir Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 曹王明，太宗第十四子。

translations.literal: Prince of Cao Ming was Taizong's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Ming, Prince of Cao, was Taizong's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十一年受封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan he received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 21 (647) he was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，賜實封八百戶，尋加滿千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was granted a substantive fief of eight hundred households; soon it was increased to a full thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 23 (649) he received a substantive fief of eight hundred households, soon increased to a full thousand.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，授梁州都督，後歷虢、蔡、蘇三州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era he was appointed Governor of Liangzhou and later successively served as Prefect of Guo, Cai, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era he was appointed governor of Liangzhou and later served successively as prefect of Guo, Cai, and Su.

sentences.zh: 詔令繼巢剌王元吉後。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to succeed Prince Cila of Chao Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to succeed Yuanji, Prince Cila of Chao.

sentences.zh: 永崇中，坐與庶人賢通謀，降封零陵王，徙於黔州。

translations.literal: In the Yongchong era, on account of plotting with the commoner Xian, he was demoted to Prince of Lingling and moved to Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchong, for plotting with the commoner Xian, he was demoted to Prince of Lingling and moved to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 都督謝祐希旨，逼脅令自殺，帝深悼之，黔府官僚咸坐免職。

translations.literal: Governor Xie You toadying to intent compelled and forced him to kill himself; the emperor deeply mourned him and Qian prefecture officials were all dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xie You, toadying to intent, compelled him to kill himself. The emperor deeply mourned him and Qian prefecture officials were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，明喪柩歸於京師，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun Ming's coffin returned to the capital and he was buried with accompaniment at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 (710) Ming's coffin returned to the capital and he was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 有二子，南州別駕零陵王俊、黎國公傑，垂拱中並遇害。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Jun, Vice-Prefect of Nan and Prince of Lingling; Jie, Duke of Li — both in the Chuigong era met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Jun, vice-prefect of Nan and Prince of Lingling; Jie, Duke of Li—both were killed in the Chuigong era.

sentences.zh: 中興初，封傑子胤為嗣曹王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration Jie's son Yin was enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration Jie's son Yin was created Heir Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 胤叔父備自南州還，又封備為嗣曹王、衛尉少卿、同正員，胤遂停封。

translations.literal: Yin's uncle Bei returned from Nan and was also enfeoffed as Heir Prince of Cao, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Regular Associate; Yin thereupon ceased enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's uncle Bei returned from Nan and was also created Heir Prince of Cao and vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, regular associate; Yin's enfeoffment ceased.

sentences.zh: 後備招慰忠州叛獠，沒於賊，又封胤為王、銀青光祿大夫、右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later Bei pacified rebellious Liao in Zhongzhou and perished at the hands of bandits; Yin was again enfeoffed as prince, Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, and General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bei pacified rebellious Liao in Zhongzhou and perished at bandit hands; Yin was again created prince, Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, and general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，子戢嗣，左衛率府中郎將。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zhan succeeded as Central Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Zhan succeeded as central commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，子皋嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Gao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Gao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 皋自有傳。

translations.literal: Gao has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太宗諸子，吳王恪、濮王泰最賢。

translations.literal: The historian says: Among Taizong's sons, Prince of Wu Ke and Prince of Pu Tai were most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Among Taizong's sons, Ke Prince of Wu and Tai Prince of Pu were the most worthy.

sentences.zh: 皆以才高辯悟，為長孫無忌忌嫉，離間父子，遽為豺狼，而無忌破家，非陰禍之報歟？

translations.literal: All because of high talent and sharp understanding, Zhangsun Wuji envied and resented them, sowed division between father and sons, and swiftly made wolves of them; yet Wuji destroyed his own house — is this not the retribution of hidden calamity?
translations.idiomatic: For their talent and brilliance Zhangsun Wuji envied them, sowed division between father and sons, and made wolves of them—yet Wuji destroyed his own house. Is this not retribution for hidden malice?

sentences.zh: 武後斫喪王室，潛移龜鼎，越王貞父子痛憤，義不圖全。

translations.literal: Empress Wu hacked away the royal house, secretly shifted the tortoise tripod; Prince of Yue Zhen father and son grieved and raged, righteousness not seeking self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu hacked at the royal house and secretly shifted the mandate; Zhen Prince of Yue and his son grieved and raged, choosing righteousness over self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 毀室之悲，《鴟鴞》之詩，傷矣！

translations.literal: The sorrow of destroying the house — the poem of The Owl — how wounding!
translations.idiomatic: The sorrow of a house destroyed—the poem of The Owl—how wounding!

sentences.zh: 比齊祐之妄作，豈同年而語哉！

translations.literal: Compared with Prince of Qi You's reckless action, how can they be spoken of in the same year?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Prince of Qi You's reckless revolt, how can they be spoken of in the same breath?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：子弟作籓，磐石維城。

translations.literal: In praise: Imperial sons made territorial princes — foundation stone, wall of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Imperial sons made territorial princes—the foundation stone, the wall of the realm.

sentences.zh: 驕侈取敗，身無令名。

translations.literal: Arrogance and extravagance bring defeat; the body wins no fine name.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance and extravagance bring defeat; the body wins no fine name.

sentences.zh: 沖、譔憤發，視死如生。

translations.literal: Chong and Shen roused in anger, viewing death as life.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Shen roused in anger, viewing death as life.

sentences.zh: 承乾、齊祐，愚弟庸兄。

translations.literal: Chengqian and Prince of Qi You — foolish younger brother, mediocre elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqian and Prince of Qi You—a foolish younger brother, a mediocre elder brother.
